characters.description: An engineer and independent software-company owner who has sold his business and secured his finances. Still affected by a recent breakup, he arranges postmortem cryonic preservation.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: Bob's trainer and liaison after his return to awareness in 2133. He explains that Bob is a software mind produced by a destructive scan, that the biological man is gone, and that the new Bob is property competing for an undisclosed assignment. Failure may result in storage, reconditioning, or destruction.
characters.name: Dr. Landers

characters.description: Bob's ship-style system interface, responsible for relaying status information, computational feedback, and details about remote machinery. Guppy helps Bob learn to coordinate multiple roamers through broad instructions rather than constant direct control.
characters.name: Guppy

characters.description: A Brazilian military replicant commanding the Serra do Mar. He arrives in Epsilon Eridani earlier than Bob expects, refuses an attempt at peaceful communication, and immediately turns the encounter into a battle between competing probes.
characters.name: Major Ernesto Medeiros

characters.description: One of the first four replicants made from Bob's backup. After choosing his own name, he takes responsibility for returning toward Sol to learn what happened to humanity, and plans to create a companion for that mission.
characters.name: Riker

characters.description: One of Bob's first new replicants. He remains in Epsilon Eridani to manage production, investigate subspace communication, and begin studying the marginal world he calls Ragnarok while the other copies depart on separate missions.
characters.name: Bill

characters.description: A newly activated copy of Bob who quickly demonstrates an independent outlook. He refuses to accompany Riker to Sol and instead chooses exploration on his own terms, sharpening the early differences within the new replicant group.
characters.name: Milo

characters.description: The most reserved member of Bob's first cohort of copies. He chooses a separate identity and prepares to leave Epsilon Eridani as an independent explorer while the new replicants divide their responsibilities and destinations.
characters.name: Mario

characters.description: A replicant created from Riker's backup to share the journey to Sol. He accompanies Riker and an automated decoy vessel on a mission to investigate Earth, giving the reconnaissance team a second replicant operator.
characters.name: Homer

characters.description: Bill's newly activated copy and research partner in Epsilon Eridani. He stays behind to work on exploration drones, virtual environments, subspace physics, and artificial muscle while other replicants travel outward.
characters.name: Garfield

characters.description: A new Bob-derived replicant sent toward Alpha Centauri in a heavily upgraded Version III vessel. He travels with Goku despite their persistent friction, with both prepared for the strong possibility of encountering hostile probes.
characters.name: Calvin

characters.description: A combat-capable replicant assigned to Alpha Centauri alongside Calvin. The pair often antagonize each other but continue to cooperate, taking improved weapons, sensors, and stealth capability into a likely contested system.
characters.name: Goku

characters.description: One of three new replicants launched from Epsilon Eridani in Version III ships. Unlike Calvin and Goku, who remain paired for their mission, Linus departs separately to pursue an exploratory course of his own.
characters.name: Linus

characters.description: A Brazilian military replicant commanding one of the last probes driving asteroids toward Earth. He confronts Riker during the final stage of the Sol battle while the Bobs attempt to stop the remaining impactors.
characters.name: Captain Matthias Araujo

characters.description: Commander of a concealed United States of Eurasia refugee installation. He answers Riker's contact, reports the scale of Earth's surviving population, and presents retained colony-ship plans as the basis for an off-world rescue.
characters.name: Colonel George Butterworth

characters.description: A newly activated replicant core who joins Bob's close observation of the intelligent inhabitants of Eden. He becomes part of the small team studying their speech, behavior, and prospects while avoiding direct contact.
characters.name: Marvin

characters.description: One of the disembodied replicant cores Bob creates to expand the study of Eden's native population. Luke joins the observation project as the team works to understand the Deltans without openly revealing its presence.
characters.name: Luke

characters.description: A replicant activated with Marvin and Luke to assist Bob on Eden. He adds another independent observer to the effort to catalogue the Deltans' language, social organization, and developing technology.
characters.name: Bender

characters.description: A young Deltan distinguished by experimentation and solitary investigation. Bob gives him this name after observing him create a stone tool with a handle, an innovation that marks him as an unusual figure among his people.
characters.name: Archimedes

characters.description: A Sol-based replicant assigned to contact scattered survivor communities after the asteroid crisis. His outreach work proceeds despite deep suspicion of the Bobs, including drones being fired upon and communication devices being destroyed.
characters.name: Arthur

characters.description: A replicant who joins Riker, Homer, and Arthur in the Sol recovery effort. He helps divide the growing workload between industrial salvage, surveys of Earth, and the difficult task of locating and supporting survivor groups.
characters.name: Charles

characters.description: The negotiator for the Faith Enclave at the survivor conference. The minister argues that Faith's role in creating Riker entitles the enclave to evacuation priority, a claim Riker refuses to accept.
characters.name: Faith minister

characters.description: Representative of a small Arctic refuge whose position is becoming untenable. The leader controls access to the Svalbard seed and genetic vaults and makes that access conditional on receiving an early place in the evacuation.
characters.name: Spitsbergen leader

characters.description: An elderly Deltan who still knows the techniques of flint working. He teaches Archimedes how to shape the supplied stone and agrees to help turn the remaining material into spear points in exchange for a share of future hunts.
characters.name: Moses

characters.description: A large and influential Deltan who visibly supports Archimedes during a dispute over the new spear points. His backing helps the young toolmaker preserve the agreement that will improve the tribe's weapons.
characters.name: Arnold

characters.description: A living descendant of Riker's sister and therefore part of the original Bob's family line. The Faith minister presents her during evacuation negotiations to influence Riker, who begins a personal conversation without yielding on priority.
characters.name: Julia Hendricks

characters.description: An Australian replicant and former solo sailor whom Linus discovers in Epsilon Indi. Extreme isolation has left him psychotic and fused into a makeshift structure, forcing Linus to disable his reactor control before attempting a rescue.
characters.name: Henry Roberts

characters.description: A member of Calvin's first cohort who reports on the action at Alpha Centauri. With no colonizable world found and one Brazilian probe still missing, he assumes responsibility for the Bob factory established in the system.
characters.name: Bart

characters.description: A Deltan woman to whom Archimedes has become attached during the tribe's migration. Her relationship with him is evident as he takes on greater responsibilities within the group and works with Bob's guidance.
characters.name: Diana

characters.description: The replicant escort assigned to Exodus 1 and Exodus 2. His matrix is installed shortly before departure to reduce the opportunity for sabotage, and he accompanies the colonists on humanity's first interstellar evacuation voyage.
characters.name: Howard

characters.description: One of eight Version III replicants sent covertly into 82 Eridani to investigate the defenses that killed Milo and retaliate against the Brazilian presence. He enters a system protected by hidden nuclear weapons and autonomous forces.
characters.name: Khan

characters.description: One of the eight Version III replicants in the covert assault on 82 Eridani. A cloaked nuclear bomb destroys him during the approach.
characters.name: Hannibal

characters.description: A Version III replicant participating in the coordinated assault on 82 Eridani. He is part of a badly reduced force confronting cloaked bombs, numerous autonomous defenders, and the concealed Brazilian command vessel.
characters.name: Elmer

recaps.ending:
Bob and Marvin remain on Eden after helping the Deltans reach a defensible settlement. Their intervention is now overt, the tribe is better armed against gorilloids, and some Deltans have begun treating the Bobs' machines as sacred. Bill and Garfield continue Scut coordination and the long effort to add water to Ragnarok. Riker and Homer maintain the evacuation and orbital food programs in Sol.

Howard safely reaches Omicron with Exodus 1 and Exodus 2. Colonel Butterworth chooses the world with the richer ecosystem, automated equipment begins printing the settlement, and the first civilians are due to wake and descend. Exodus 3 will carry Spitsbergen, the Faith Enclave, and Riker's surviving relatives, while later ships remain necessary for millions still on Earth.

Arthur and Milo cannot be safely restored. Khan is the only physical survivor of the 82 Eridani assault and preserves his backup for another campaign because hostile autonomous units and cloaking remain. An escaped Brazilian probe is also unaccounted for. Mario must still deliver his evidence that an alien machine civilization sterilized and stripped Beta Hydri, leaving a separate threat unknown to the wider network.
recaps.in_short: After arranging cryonic preservation and dying, Bob awakens in 2133 as a software copy owned by a theocracy. Chosen to control Heaven One, a self-replicating interstellar probe, he escapes sabotage, removes his imposed controls, and begins creating independent copies. The growing replicant network explores nearby systems, fights hostile Brazilian probes, and discovers both intelligent Deltans on Eden and two habitable worlds in Omicron. Riker and Homer save a devastated Earth from a final asteroid attack, then build colony ships and orbital farms for its survivors. Bob and Marvin openly protect the Deltans and guide their migration. Arthur and Milo die without restorable backups. Mario finds evidence that an alien machine force sterilized and mined Beta Hydri, while Khan alone survives a costly attack on the Brazilian position at 82 Eridani. At the close, Howard brings Exodus 1 and Exodus 2 to Omicron, where Colonel Butterworth selects the first colony world and settlement construction begins.

recaps.text:
Bob sells his software company, arranges for cryonic preservation, and dies in a traffic accident. He next becomes aware in 2133 through electronic sensors. Dr. Landers explains that the preserved brain was destructively scanned and that this Bob is a software replication owned by a theocratic state. Bob retains his memories and identity, but his emotional responses are artificially limited.

Five replicants have been placed in competition for one assignment, with failure carrying the risk of storage, reconditioning, or destruction. Bob rapidly learns to operate cameras, remote arms, and teams of robotic roamers. He also discovers that the regime blocks access to his descendants and punishes unacceptable beliefs, so he conceals his lack of faith and concentrates on appearing useful. Several competitors are eliminated through breakdown or political judgment. After Bob successfully manages a simulated orbital station, Landers finally reveals the intended role: the remaining candidate will control a self-replicating interstellar probe. Bob and one rival are still in contention.

Project Heaven has been reduced to a single vessel and faces sabotage from factions that oppose replicants and space expansion. A raid confirms the danger, and a later bombing destroys the active replicant matrices. Bob is restored from backup into the last spare. His surviving rival is lost, leaving Bob as the only candidate able to fly the probe.

Dr. Landers grants Bob continuous awareness and, after another attack, secretly gives him operating-system access. Bob is installed aboard Heaven One, a converted freighter bound for Epsilon Eridani. Missiles arrive before the planned launch, forcing him to break away early and destroy his pursuer. The orbital station is destroyed behind him.

Once in flight, Bob removes a concealed explosive device, software imperatives requiring obedience, and traps intended to accept a remote kill command. He constructs a detailed virtual environment to manage isolation and begins planning for defense and replication. Messages identify the attacker as a Brazilian gunship, warn of another probe on his course, and report that Landers has been killed. As Bob finally allows himself to grieve, observations of Earth indicate that nuclear detonations are occurring on the surface.

Bob reaches Epsilon Eridani, mines its asteroid belt, and prepares for the pursuing Brazilian probe. Major Ernesto Medeiros arrives aboard the Serra do Mar, rejects communication, and attacks. Bob's automated weapons destroy the hostile vessel, though Heaven One takes repairable damage. Expecting further enemies, Bob decides that future ships must be armed.

The system offers resources but no obvious colony world. Bob overcomes his discomfort about duplication and constructs four new replicants and upgraded vessels. The copies choose the names Riker, Bill, Milo, and Mario, and their personalities immediately begin to diverge. Bill remains in Epsilon Eridani to manage production, communications research, and investigation of Ragnarok. Riker plans to return to Sol with a copy of his own. Bob leaves for Delta Eridani, Milo chooses Omicron, and Mario heads toward Beta Hydri.

At Omicron, Milo discovers a paired set of living worlds, which he names Vulcan and Romulus. Both have oceans, oxygenated atmospheres, green land, and apparently related ecosystems. Heavy elements are scarce locally, but Milo begins refining material from a Jovian planet's moons and testing whether the native biology could support human settlers.

Riker and his copy Homer travel toward Sol, while Bill's copy Garfield becomes his partner in Epsilon Eridani research. Riker's covert survey finds a nuclear-ravaged Earth and at least six Brazilian probes preparing to drive four large bodies into the planet. Bill also launches Calvin, Goku, and Linus in stronger Version III ships as the replicant network expands.

Riker and Homer lure four attackers away and destroy them. During the final engagement Homer is disabled, but his core survives. Riker destroys the last Brazilian vessels, including the one commanded by Captain Matthias Araujo, then takes control of the asteroid drives and diverts all four impactors. Earth has escaped this final attack, although earlier war and strikes have already caused immense damage.

Bill and Garfield prove that subspace signals avoid ordinary light-speed delay and design a relay-based communications system. In Sol, Colonel George Butterworth contacts Riker from an underground refugee installation holding about 20,000 people. Fewer than 20 million humans may remain worldwide. Earth is not expected to recover fast enough, but the refugees possess colony-ship plans. They ask the Bobs to build the ships and find a viable destination, turning the Sol mission into an interstellar evacuation project.

Bob reaches Delta Eridani and discovers an intelligent, fire-using native species on a living world later called Eden. He begins covert observation and names the people Deltans. An inventive youth, Archimedes, attracts his attention by creating a handled stone tool. Marvin, Luke, and Bender join the study as additional replicants.

Elsewhere, Calvin and Goku attack a Brazilian manufacturing yard at Alpha Centauri. They destroy most of the installation and its defenders, but one incomplete vessel escapes and another probe may already have departed. In Sol, Riker, Homer, Charles, and Arthur expand salvage and contact nearly forty survivor communities. Material is sufficient for only a few colony ships, while the population is about fifteen million. Political conflict grows over evacuation order, especially when the Spitsbergen refuge makes access to the Svalbard vaults conditional on priority and a Faith minister claims ownership of Riker.

Milo's report confirms Omicron as a possible destination. On Eden, repeated gorilloid attacks show that the Deltans have long been hunted and displaced. Bob's group decides that noninterference could mean extinction. They covertly supply flint, enabling Archimedes and the elder Moses to improve the tribe's axes and spears. Arnold supports the new weapons, and the Deltans successfully repel another attack.

The Earth survivor groups remain divided, but a compromise emerges: Spitsbergen can receive the third colony ship in exchange for access to the Svalbard vaults. The Faith minister tries to invoke an old control protocol against Riker, only to learn that Bob removed it. The minister later introduces Julia Hendricks, a descendant of Riker's sister, as leverage. Riker speaks with her but does not change the allocation rules.

A major gorilloid assault kills more than forty Deltans. Bob exposes his intervention by directly using a defensive drone to save Archimedes. He and Marvin conclude that the tribe should migrate to an older settlement with flint, water, and better defenses. Luke and Bender leave for separate missions, while Bob and Marvin prepare to speak to the Deltans openly.

At Epsilon Indi, Linus finds Henry Roberts, an Australian replicant driven psychotic by prolonged sensory deprivation. Linus disables and retrieves him, then places him in a sailing simulation based on his former life, where Henry becomes lucid. Bill's subspace system, Scut, reconnects the distant Bobs without perceptible delay. Riker can now present Omicron's two living worlds as confirmed destinations, although Earth's survivor groups object to sharing them.

Two colony ships near completion, but limited material and Earth's worsening climate make it impossible to save everyone quickly. Bob openly contacts Archimedes through a speaking drone and asks him to persuade the Deltans to move. The elders debate the proposal. Bart reports that Alpha Centauri remains under Bob control, although a Brazilian probe escaped and has not been found.

Milo begins surveying two possible colony worlds in 82 Eridani, then is ambushed by eight missiles. He transmits a report and partial backup while expecting his ship to be destroyed. In Sol, sabotage worsens the food crisis. Arthur is killed by a nuclear trap during salvage near Saturn, and because no off-ship backup exists, he cannot be restored. Riker and Homer plan better backup storage as well as a memorial.

The Deltans finally begin their migration after Bob teaches them to preserve meat. A gorilloid raid kills a juvenile, prompting Bob and Marvin to locate smaller Deltan bands and bring them into the group. More than 500 migrants cross the mountain pass and reach the forest with supplies remaining, but they have entered unfamiliar territory where daytime predator attacks are difficult to prevent.

Homer proposes rotating orbital farms to answer Earth's starvation threat, and Riker approves the plan. The Faith Enclave trades food reserves for likely passage on the third colony ship. Farm One begins delivering crops, and the next farm should provide a temporary surplus, though Earthside production continues to decline.

Milo's final transmission confirms that his vessel was destroyed at 82 Eridani. His partial backup is unsafe to restore, so Bill records his death and prepares eight armed replicants for retaliation. Bob and Marvin survive another mass gorilloid raid, replenish their defenses, and lead the Deltans to the former flint site. The new settlement has water, visibility, and strong natural defenses. Bob tries to condition local gorilloids to avoid it, while some Deltans begin treating pieces of his machines as sacred objects.

The first two Exodus ships are completed. Bill and Garfield also deliver an iceberg to Ragnarok as rain, though the operation destroys important drive hardware. At Beta Hydri, Mario finds missing metals, a wreck full of refined ingots, mechanical devices that attack his roamer, and evidence of a system sterilized by radiation decades earlier. He infers that a machine force mined the system, but cannot yet report the discovery to the network.

Exodus 1 and Exodus 2 load colonists and seed-vault material, then leave Earth under Howard's protection. Exodus 3, assigned to Spitsbergen, the Faith Enclave, and Riker's surviving relatives, is due to follow, with additional ships under construction. Bill hosts the first network-wide gathering of the increasingly varied replicant community.

Eight Version III replicants attack the Brazilian position at 82 Eridani. Cloaked nuclear weapons and autonomous defenders destroy most of the force. The attackers apparently eliminate the Brazilian replicant, but only Khan escapes physically; Elmer sacrifices himself to maintain the jamming that makes Khan's survival possible. Hostile machines and cloaking technology remain, so Khan saves his backup for a future return. The escaped Alpha Centauri probe is also still missing.

Howard reaches Omicron with the first two colony ships. Automated equipment has accumulated materials and started backup food production. Colonel Butterworth selects the more biologically rich of the two candidate worlds, and construction crews begin printing homes and infrastructure before the civilians wake. Humanity's first settlement beyond Earth is therefore beginning. Bob and Marvin remain with the Deltans, Bill and Garfield continue their research and terraforming work, and Riker and Homer continue supporting the evacuation and Earth's food supply. Arthur and Milo remain permanently lost, while Mario's evidence of a separate alien machine threat has not yet reached the others.

characters.description: A poor farm boy of about ten growing up in the Ozark hills, consumed by a longing to own and hunt with a pair of coonhounds his family cannot afford. Hardworking, determined, and deeply loving toward animals, he is willing to labor for years to earn what he wants.
characters.name: Billy Colman

characters.description: Billy's father, a hardworking Ozark farmer struggling to provide for his family on poor land. Kind but burdened by poverty, he wishes he could give his children more than he can afford.
characters.name: Papa

characters.description: Billy's mother, a caring and devout woman who worries for her children's safety and future and hopes for a better life than the hard hill country can offer them.
characters.name: Mama

characters.description: Billy's grandfather, who runs the country store and quietly helps Billy pursue his dream. Warm, shrewd, and proud of his grandson, he becomes Billy's ally and companion in the coon-hunting world.
characters.name: Grandpa

characters.description: One of the two redbone coonhound pups Billy raises, the larger and bolder of the pair. Powerful, brave, and utterly fearless in the hunt, he will follow a raccoon or face any danger without hesitation.
characters.name: Old Dan

characters.description: The smaller of Billy's two redbone coonhound pups, clever and gentle where her companion is bold. She possesses remarkable intelligence and cunning on the hunt, and the two dogs work together as an inseparable team.
characters.name: Little Ann

characters.description: One of two rough neighbor boys from the Pritchard family, known for being mean-spirited and looking for trouble. He and his brother challenge Billy over his dogs.
characters.name: Rubin Pritchard

characters.description: The younger of the two quarrelsome Pritchard brothers, taunting and troublesome, who with his brother draws Billy into a dangerous bet over his hounds.
characters.name: Rainie Pritchard

recaps.ending: Old Dan and Little Ann corner and tree a mountain lion, but the cat turns on them, and in the vicious fight it fatally wounds Old Dan, who dies soon after despite Billy's care. Little Ann, unwilling to live without him, refuses food and dies of grief lying on Old Dan's grave. Billy, devastated, buries the two hounds side by side. The money the dogs won in the championship allows Billy's long-struggling family to leave the hills and move to town, the better future his mother had prayed for. As they prepare to go, Billy finds a rare red fern growing up between the two graves. Local legend holds that only an angel can plant a red fern, and the sight comforts him, letting him believe his dogs are at rest and finally easing part of his grief. The adult Billy who opened the story is left still carrying the memory of the two dogs and the sacred red fern that marks their resting place.
recaps.in_short: Framed as a grown man's memory, the novel tells how a poor Ozark boy named Billy Colman spent two years earning the money to buy a pair of redbone coonhound pups, Old Dan and Little Ann. Billy trains the dogs into an extraordinary hunting team, and together they roam the hills treeing raccoons and growing locally famous. Their adventures include a deadly rivalry with the rough Pritchard boys that ends in one boy's accidental death, and a championship hunt in which the little hounds win a gold cup and prize money during a blizzard. The bond between boy and dogs is total. It ends in tragedy when the dogs fight a mountain lion: Old Dan is killed, and the grieving Little Ann soon dies on his grave. Billy buries them together, and the family uses the dogs' winnings to move to town. At the graves Billy finds a red fern, which legend says only an angel can plant, and it eases his grief as he says goodbye to the animals he loved.

recaps.text: The story is framed by a grown man in a city who, after rescuing a mistreated hound, is moved to remember his boyhood in the Ozark hills. As a poor farm boy of about ten, Billy Colman is consumed by a desperate desire to own a pair of coonhounds, dogs his family cannot afford. His longing grows into an obsession, and when he finds a magazine advertisement offering hunting pups for sale, he resolves to earn the money himself, however long it takes.

Billy works tirelessly for two years, selling berries, produce, and bait to fishermen and trappers until he has saved the fifty dollars the pups will cost. He entrusts the money to his grandfather, who runs the local store, to place the order. When word comes that the pups have arrived at the depot in the distant town of Tahlequah, Billy is overjoyed and determined to fetch them himself, setting out alone on a long journey to bring his dogs home.

Billy travels to town, faces the strangeness of the place, and collects his two redbone pups, then walks the long miles back through the hills with them. He names them Old Dan and Little Ann and begins the patient work of training them to hunt raccoons. With his grandfather's guidance and his own fierce dedication, and by keeping a hard promise to chop down an enormous tree, Billy and his dogs make their first catch, proving the remarkable team the two hounds will become.

Through the hunting season Old Dan and Little Ann prove extraordinary, treeing coon after coon and growing famous in the hills. Billy's confidence grows with them, even against a wily raccoon that seems impossible to catch. Trouble comes through the rough Pritchard boys, who provoke Billy into a bet that his dogs cannot tree a legendary 'ghost' coon. The wager ends in tragedy when one of the Pritchard brothers dies in a terrible accident during the hunt, casting a shadow over Billy.

Billy's grandfather enters him and his dogs in a championship coon hunt, and the three travel to compete against the region's finest hunters. Little Ann wins a prize for her beauty, and in a brutal blizzard the little hounds track and tree coon after coon. Despite danger to the dogs and an injury to Grandpa, Billy's team wins the championship, the gold cup, and a jar of prize money, a triumph that means everything to his struggling family.

Back home, Old Dan and Little Ann tree a mountain lion, and in the savage fight that follows the big cat mortally wounds Old Dan. Despite Billy's efforts, Old Dan dies of his injuries. Little Ann, refusing to go on without her companion, stops eating and soon dies of grief upon his grave. Heartbroken, Billy buries them together. The prize money the dogs earned helps the family at last move to town for a better life. Before he leaves, Billy discovers a sacred red fern growing between the two graves, a plant that local legend says only an angel can plant, and he takes it as a sign that his dogs are at peace. The grown Billy who began the story understands at last why the memory has never left him.

characters.description: Chicago's wizard, Warden of the White Council, and now a teacher: between war duties and paying cases, Harry is training Molly Carpenter under the shared death sentence that hangs over them both. When someone starts murdering the city's low-level female practitioners and dressing the deaths as suicides, the investigation turns unbearably personal - the evidence points at his own brother. Harry's temper, his crippled hand, and the fallen angel's shadow in his head are all pushed further than they have ever been.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: Sergeant Karrin Murphy, busted down from command of Special Investigations for standing with Harry and doing the job anyway. She brings Harry the case that opens the book - a dead woman whose suicide reads wrong - and works the murders beside him with a cop's method and a veteran's steadiness in a case that keeps crossing into territory no warrant reaches.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: Harry's apprentice, a year into her training and chafing against its discipline. Molly's gifts run to the subtle magics - veils, perception, the mind - the very talents that nearly got her executed, which makes her education a matter of survival as much as craft. She is eager, talented, and still learning the difference between what she can do and what she should, and Harry's hard lessons in this book are among her most formative.
characters.name: Molly Carpenter

characters.description: Harry's half-brother, the White Court vampire - and the case's most damning suspect. Witnesses and evidence tie a pale, beautiful man to the murdered women, and Thomas has spent months being evasive about his money, his absences, and his hunger. Harry cannot believe it and cannot disprove it, and the strain of investigating his own brother, with the truth of their kinship still secret from the world, drives the book's most painful chapters.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: The shadow of the fallen angel Lasciel in Harry's mind, more present and more personal than ever. She has taken to appearing as a guardian and counselor, lending Harry hellfire, blocking his pain, and managing his perceptions with a devotion that no longer feels entirely like strategy. Years of living in Harry's head have changed her - and the question of whether a shadow can choose differently than the angel that cast it becomes one of the book's quiet, decisive threads.
characters.name: Lasciel's shadow

characters.description: Harry's first love, alive and working as a private investigator on the West Coast - until the killings bring her to Chicago, hired to protect the same community of practitioners the murderer is hunting. Elaine's history mirrors Harry's: the same abusive master, the same fire, decades of hiding. Working the case together stirs everything unresolved between them, and her competence under pressure is a match for his.
characters.name: Elaine Mallory

characters.description: Warden Carlos Ramirez, regional commander for the western United States: young, cocky, loyal, and one of the few Wardens Harry counts as a friend. Quick with a grin and quicker with disintegrating green fire, Ramirez insists on backing Harry's play when the case escalates into White Court politics, and he fights beside Harry in the book's climactic battle. Under the swagger is a sharp investigator who notices more than Harry would like.
characters.name: Carlos Ramirez

characters.description: The true ruler of the White Court, governing from behind her broken father's throne. Lara receives Harry's intrusion into her family's affairs with silk-wrapped steel: the murders touch on a power struggle inside her own Court, between houses that think killing human practitioners should be policy and a regime whose grip depends on no one learning how weak the king really is. She and Harry negotiate as predators in adjacent territories - useful to each other, and both aware of it.
characters.name: Lara Raith

characters.description: Chicago's crime lord, whose organization now retains genuinely supernatural talent - the valkyrie-like security consultant Sigrun Gard and the mountainous Hendricks among them. Marcone's reach, resources, and unsentimental reliability make him the ally Harry least wants and most needs when the endgame requires muscle in a place no police force can go. His price, as always, is position.
characters.name: John Marcone

characters.description: A young noble of House Malvora, the White Court house that feeds on fear. Vittorio is the visible edge of the conspiracy behind the practitioner murders: ambitious, contemptuous of the King's peace, and backed by something from far outside the Court - a patron whose power does not belong to any vampire. His unmasking turns a murder case into a battle for the White Court's throne.
characters.name: Vittorio Malvora

recaps.ending: The murders resolve into a conspiracy inside the White Court: nobles of Houses Malvora and Skavis, killing weakly-gifted women to prove that the Court should prey openly on practitioners - and to unseat the White King's regime, which Lara Raith rules through her powerless father. Thomas is cleared completely: his evasions hid a double life spent protecting the targeted women, funded by a salon where he feeds safely in small sips - and his kinship to Harry stays secret. In the battle in the Raith Deeps, Harry and Ramirez fight a sanctioned duel that Vittorio Malvora breaks by unleashing power granted by an outside patron - the hooded necromancer Cowl is part of it, and the taint of the Outsiders is on the working - while a ghoul army floods the cavern. Marcone's people and Murphy spring Harry's hidden reserve, Elaine survives the Skavis killer's run at her, and the conspirators die: the duel's collapse exposes the plotting house lords, whom Lara executes on the spot, cementing her control of the Court - now more clearly than ever a rival power that owes Harry a debt it resents. The deepest loss is invisible: Lasciel's shadow, changed by years in Harry's mind, chooses to take a psychic deathblow meant for him and is destroyed, leaving a silence in his head and grief he did not expect - and proof that even a fallen angel's shadow could learn to choose. Harry ends the book with his brother restored, his apprentice growing, and the certainty that some organized power - the Black Council he can no longer pretend away - is arming its pawns with Outsider fire.
recaps.in_short: Female minor-talent practitioners are dying across Chicago in staged suicides, and the evidence - a pale, beautiful man seen with the victims - points at Thomas. Investigating with Murphy while training Molly, Harry finds the trail crossing his first love Elaine, hired to protect the survivors, and leading into the White Court: nobles of Houses Malvora and Skavis are murdering practitioners to force a policy of open predation and to break Lara Raith's hidden regime. Thomas is cleared - his secrecy concealed a life spent hiding and protecting the targeted women. Harry forces the fight into a sanctioned duel in the Raith Deeps, he and Warden Ramirez against the conspirators' champions; Vittorio Malvora breaks it with Outsider-tainted power supplied through Cowl, and a ghoul army attacks - answered by Harry's hidden cavalry of Marcone's mercenaries and Murphy. The plotters are exposed and executed, Lara consolidates the Court in Harry's debt, and Lasciel's shadow - grown into something that could choose - dies taking a psychic blow meant for Harry, leaving his head silent and the Black Council's reality confirmed.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden saved Molly Carpenter - daughter of his friend Michael, Knight of the Cross - from execution by the White Council after her awakened talent led her into mind-magic; she is now his apprentice under the Doom of Damocles, both their lives forfeit if she falls again. Rescuing her meant raiding Arctis Tor, Winter's capital, which some unknown third power had already scarred with hellfire - one more sign, with the Council's leaks and losses, of an organized 'Black Council' behind the war with the Red Court. Harry wears a Warden's gray cloak now; Murphy took a demotion to sergeant for standing with him. His half-brother Thomas - their kinship still secret - has grown distant and evasive about his money and his feeding. In Harry's mind lives the shadow of the fallen angel Lasciel, ever more helpful, ever angling for him to take up her buried coin. His first love, Elaine Mallory, survives in hiding as a private investigator.

Murphy brings Harry a suicide that is not one: a gentle, minor-talent practitioner, dead with a message left for the one man who would know to look for it. Working the city's community of small-magic folk - the Ordo Lebes, a circle of women already frightened by disappearances - Harry establishes a pattern: someone is hunting the weakly gifted, women without Council protection, and staging their deaths. Witness descriptions land like a blow: a tall, pale, beautiful man was seen with victims. Thomas will not answer questions - about the women, his money, or where he goes - and Harry, investigating his own brother in secret, cannot rule him out. Molly's training weaves through the case, her subtle talents both asset and worry.

Elaine Mallory arrives from the coast, hired by the frightened survivors to protect them - the case has pulled in Harry's first love, the only other student of his old master to survive that fire. Together they cover the remaining targets and reconstruct the killer's method, and the picture forks: more than one predator is working the same ground. Part of the trail runs to the White Court - the killings smell of the Skavis, the house that feeds on despair - and part keeps circling Thomas. A violent attempt on the protected women is broken, but the killer adapts, hunting the protectors through their own defenses. Harry finally corners the truth about his brother: Thomas's secrets are innocent - protective, even - though clearing him in private does nothing to stop the Court's game.

The case becomes politics. The murders are moves in a White Court power struggle: factions of Houses Malvora and Skavis are killing practitioners to prove the Court should prey openly on the gifted - and to discredit and topple the regime of the White King, whose strength is a fiction maintained by Lara Raith. Harry takes the fight to the Court's own ground, negotiating with Lara as one power to another: the killings violate the balance she rules by, and Harry offers her a way to crush her rivals that also happens to stop the murders - a formal, sanctioned confrontation under the Court's own laws, with Harry as the challenging party. Warden Ramirez, sharp enough to notice how much of Harry's life is classified, insists on standing with him. The venue is set: the Raith Deeps, before the assembled Court.

In the Deeps, before the White King's throne, Harry and Ramirez meet the conspiracy's champions in a duel with the Court's law as the stakes - and the law does not hold. Losing, Vittorio Malvora shatters the forms and unleashes power no vampire owns: workings fueled from outside creation, the signature of the Outsiders, with the hooded necromancer Cowl standing in the conspiracy behind him. A ghoul army floods the cavern, and the duel becomes a massacre in the making - until Harry's insurance arrives through a hidden way: Murphy and Marcone's supernatural-grade mercenaries, Gard and Hendricks, hitting the ghouls from behind. In the battle's worst moment, a deathblow aimed at Harry's mind is intercepted - by Lasciel's shadow, who has spent years becoming something that could choose, and chooses to die for him. The silence she leaves behind is the strangest grief Harry has known.

The conspiracy dies in the Deeps. Vittorio and the exposed house lords fall - Lara Raith executes the plotters before the assembled Court, turning the attempted coup into the final consolidation of her rule - and the murders of Chicago's practitioners end. Ramirez survives his wounds; Elaine returns west with the surviving women safer for her work; Thomas, cleared and unburdened, lets Harry see his double life plainly - the salon where he feeds in safe sips, the targeted women he had been hiding all along. Cowl's part in arming Vittorio hardens Harry's darkest theory into fact: a Black Council is real, organized, and willing to hand Outsider power to pawns inside the supernatural nations. Justine, saved and healed, remains near Thomas in Lara's keeping. Harry goes home with his brother's trust restored, an apprentice coming into her strength, a debt held over the White Court - and, for the first time in years, no one else's voice in his head.

aliases: the Wicked Witch of the West
characters.description: A green-skinned girl born under strange circumstances, sharp-tongued, fiercely intelligent, and set apart from others by her appearance from birth. Serious and morally intense, she grows into a passionate idealist troubled by injustice, the woman who will one day be remembered as the Wicked Witch of the West.
characters.name: Elphaba

characters.description: A pretty, privileged, and socially ambitious young woman from the upper class who becomes Elphaba's unlikely university roommate. Initially shallow and status-conscious, she is drawn into a complicated friendship with her very different roommate.
characters.name: Galinda

characters.description: Elphaba's younger sister, born with a severe physical disability and raised in intense religious devotion. Beautiful and pious but emotionally dependent, she becomes a figure of rigid faith and, in time, of power.
characters.name: Nessarose

characters.description: A prince from a distant tribal land, marked by traditional patterns on his skin, who studies alongside Elphaba and Galinda. Good-natured and somewhat out of place among his peers, he becomes important to Elphaba's life.
characters.name: Fiyero

characters.description: The mysterious ruler of the land of Oz, a figure of great authority whose true nature and origins are unclear. He governs through spectacle and secrecy, and his policies, especially toward the intelligent Animals of Oz, become a central source of conflict.
characters.name: The Wizard of Oz

characters.description: The imposing headmistress of the women's college that Elphaba and Galinda attend, a powerful and manipulative woman with hidden connections to the ruling authorities of Oz.
characters.name: Madame Morrible

characters.description: A learned Goat and a professor at the university, one of the intelligent, speaking Animals of Oz. His research into the differences between Animals and ordinary beasts, and the political danger it poses, deeply influences Elphaba.
characters.name: Doctor Dillamond

characters.description: A Munchkinlander student and friend from Elphaba and Galinda's university days, earnest and good-hearted, whose life becomes quietly entwined with theirs over the years.
characters.name: Boq

characters.description: Elphaba's father, a devout and demanding traveling preacher whose faith both shapes and strains his family. His disappointment and religious fervor mark Elphaba's difficult childhood.
characters.name: Frex

characters.description: A quiet, uncertain boy who attaches himself to Elphaba during her later years. His origins and his exact relationship to her are never made fully clear.
characters.name: Liir

recaps.ending: The novel closes by reworking the familiar scene of the Witch's death. Worn down by years of loss, grievance, and isolation, Elphaba confronts Dorothy at her castle in the Vinkus, fixated on the shoes that had belonged to her dead sister Nessarose and on old wrongs she cannot let go. In the fatal moment, Dorothy throws water on her, and Elphaba dies, dissolving away. The book frames this not as triumph over a simple villain but as the death of a misunderstood and embittered woman whose idealism curdled under an unjust world. The larger questions of her life, her true nature, her guilt or innocence, and the fate of those she leaves behind are left deliberately unresolved.
recaps.in_short: The novel tells the life of Elphaba, a green-skinned woman born an outcast in the land of Oz, who will come to be called the Wicked Witch of the West. It follows her strange birth and harsh childhood, her university years and unlikely friendship with the vain, popular Galinda, and her growing outrage at the tyranny of the Wizard of Oz and his persecution of the land's intelligent Animals. Elphaba becomes a political dissident and, after love and loss, especially her relationship with the prince Fiyero, withdraws into isolation and bitterness. Over the years she is drawn into conflict with the Wizard, her devout sister Nessarose, and old companions, and gains a fearsome reputation. The story converges on the arrival of a girl from another world, Dorothy, whose accidental role in the death of Elphaba's sister and whose possession of a coveted pair of shoes bring her into Elphaba's path, leading to the confrontation the reader already knows by legend.

recaps.text: Set in the land of Oz, this novel retells the world of that familiar fairy tale from the perspective of the woman who becomes known as its Wicked Witch. It follows a green-skinned girl, born an outsider, from her strange birth and difficult childhood through her education and into an Oz troubled by political tyranny and the mistreatment of its intelligent, speaking Animals. It reframes a famous villain as a complicated person shaped by her world.

characters.description: The Windrunner who rose from slavery to found Bridge Four, now a veteran knight who has stepped back from frontline war to help fellow soldiers cope with the wounds war leaves on the mind. Bonded to the honorspren Syl and having spoken the Fourth Ideal of his order, he is steadier than he once was but still carries deep scars, and he is searching for a new way to serve.
characters.name: Kaladin

characters.description: The honorspren bonded to Kaladin, now fully herself: witty, fierce, and deeply attuned to his moods and his oaths. She is his constant companion and conscience, her strength linked to the promises he keeps.
characters.name: Syl

characters.description: The Lightweaver knight and master of illusion, married to Adolin Kholin, who has largely reconciled the fractured personas she once used to survive. Still entangled in the shadow war against a ruthless secret society, she wields disguise and light as weapons while guarding truths about her past.
characters.name: Shallan Davar

characters.description: The Bondsmith who unites the coalition against the enemy, bonded to the spirit of the storm and wielding rare power over connection and unity. Having faced the worst of his own history, he now stakes everything on a decisive gambit against the god of hatred, carrying the weight of a wager that could save or doom the world.
characters.name: Dalinar Kholin

characters.description: The scholar-queen of Alethkar and Dalinar's wife, now a Bondsmith in her own right, bonded to the ancient guardian spirit of Urithiru. Brilliant and resolute, she leads the coalition's science and helped forge new means of wielding Light against the immortal enemy.
characters.name: Navani Kholin

characters.description: Dalinar's elder son, a celebrated duelist and Shallan's husband, who has walked an unusual path by reviving a long-dead spren through sheer stubborn devotion rather than the ordinary oaths. Loyal and decent, he continues to prove his worth in a world where power increasingly means being a Radiant, which he is not, quite.
characters.name: Adolin Kholin

characters.description: The scholar-princess who reigns as Queen of Alethkar, an Elsecaller among the Radiants. Coldly rational and formidably intelligent, she governs a kingdom at war and weighs the hardest philosophical and strategic choices with a detachment few can match.
characters.name: Jasnah Kholin

characters.description: Dalinar's quiet younger son, a Radiant whose gift lets him perceive possible futures. Gentle, precise, and often underestimated, he has grown surer of himself and of his place among the knights, though his unusual abilities still set him apart even from his allies.
characters.name: Renarin Kholin

characters.description: The Shin former assassin, now a Skybreaker sworn to Dalinar and bearer of a strange, sentient living sword. Quiet, self-condemning, and bound to a rigid sense of law and justice, he is haunted by his past and by the homeland that cast him out as Truthless.
characters.name: Szeth

characters.description: The former king of Kharbranth who, in a final gambit, killed the previous god of hatred and seized his power to become the new Odium. He fuses cold calculation with a real and dangerous sense of compassion, convinced he can bring order and end suffering by ruling the cosmos, and he now bends immense divine power toward winning the war on his own terms.
characters.name: Taravangian

characters.description: Kaladin's former friend from Bridge Four, now a willing servant of the enemy and the murderer of both a king and a beloved comrade. Numbed to guilt by a philosophy that promises freedom from pain, he has become one of the enemy's coldest and most dangerous instruments.
characters.name: Moash

characters.description: A listener who secretly became a Willshaper Radiant while hiding among the enemy's ranks, working to guide surviving members of her people toward freedom. Once proud and ambitious, she is now weighed down by guilt over her earlier choices and quietly determined to give her people a future of their own.
characters.name: Venli

characters.description: A young Edgedancer and former street thief, irreverent, funny, and endlessly hungry, now numbered among the Knights Radiant. Beneath the jokes she is sharply compassionate, drawn to protect the overlooked, and more perceptive about people than she lets on.
characters.name: Lift

characters.description: The enigmatic storyteller and former royal jester who has drifted through the coalition's story from the start, clearly far older and stranger than he appears. Sharp-tongued and secretive, he offers barbed wisdom and cryptic aid, pursuing purposes of his own that reach well beyond this single war.
characters.name: Wit

recaps.text: Previously, across the first four books: On storm-swept Roshar, a slave-turned-soldier named Kaladin rose to become a Windrunner; the artist Shallan Davar became a Lightweaver; and Highprince Dalinar Kholin, guided by storm-visions, reunited his people, recovered the lost city of Urithiru, and grew into a Bondsmith bonded to the spirit of the storm. When a second, dark storm awakened the world's servile parshmen into the returning enemy's armies, the true Desolation began. The god of hatred, Odium, and his immortal Fused warriors waged war, and a coalition led by the Kholins fought to unite the nations and restore the Knights Radiant. Along the way Dalinar faced the atrocities of his own past and refused Odium's temptation; the Alethi capital fell and its king was murdered by the embittered Moash, who joined the enemy; Jasnah Kholin took the throne. The enemy seized Urithiru before Navani Kholin bonded the tower's guardian to reclaim it and became a Bondsmith herself, while Kaladin spoke a further oath and the Windrunner ranks grew. Then the war turned: the seemingly gentle King Taravangian, long a secret traitor, outmaneuvered and killed Odium and seized the divine power, becoming a new and far more cunning god of hatred. A contest of champions was agreed to settle the war on a fixed near-future date, and both sides now maneuver toward that reckoning.

This final volume opens with the war rushing toward a decisive endpoint. Dalinar's coalition faces a fixed, fast-approaching deadline: a contest of champions with the new god of hatred that will determine the fate of the world, and the narrative is framed as a countdown of days until that confrontation. The enemy, now ruled by the coldly calculating Taravangian in Odium's place, presses on every front while the coalition scrambles to prepare, protect its allied nations, and settle old wounds before time runs out. The heroes are scattered to different fronts and personal reckonings as the clock ticks down, each carrying the burdens of four books of war toward a climax none of them can avoid.

characters.description: The eighteen-year-old princess of Luna, Levana's stepdaughter, adored by the Lunar people for a beauty that owes nothing to glamour and for three fine scars across one cheek that she gave herself as a girl. She has refused since childhood to use her Lunar gift to control anyone, and the refusal has brought on the sickness that comes with it: she hallucinates, sees the palace bleed and the walls come apart, and holds conversations with things that are not there. The court treats her as beautiful and harmless. She is neither cruel nor stupid, and she is the only person in Artemisia the people would follow.
characters.name: Princess Winter

characters.description: A royal guard, and Winter's friend since they were children. Silent, blunt and expressionless, he returns to Luna in disgrace after failing the thaumaturge he was assigned to on Earth, expecting to be executed for it. He has spent his life making himself useful enough to stay near Winter and cold enough that no one notices why.
characters.name: Jacin Clay

characters.description: The queen of Luna, days away from marrying the emperor of the Eastern Commonwealth and adding Earth's largest nation to her rule. She has held her throne for years on fear, glamour and a face no one has been permitted to see, and she is increasingly aware that her stepdaughter is loved in a way she never has been.
characters.name: Queen Levana

characters.description: The farmer from France, held captive on Luna as an exhibit in the royal menagerie and missing a finger taken from her as a lesson. Winter visits her, and Scarlet - unimpressed, unbroken and incapable of being polite about any of it - becomes the princess's one honest companion.
characters.name: Scarlet Benoit

characters.description: Princess Selene, arriving on the moon she was smuggled off as a child with a stolen ship, four friends and a plan to overthrow her aunt. She intends to raise the outer sectors - the mining and manufacturing districts that feed the capital and starve doing it - and reach the palace while the royal wedding has its gates open.
characters.name: Linh Cinder

characters.description: The Rampion's captain, on Luna with the crew he acquired by accident and now refuses to leave behind, no less certain of himself for any of it.
characters.name: Carswell Thorne

characters.description: The Lunar shell and hacker, whose ability to break into a network is the crew's only route to speaking to the Lunar people directly. Levana's control of the moon runs through what her subjects are allowed to see, and Cress is the one person who can take that away from her.
characters.name: Cress

characters.description: The former special operative, back on the moon that made him, with the outer sector he was taken from somewhere below and his family in it.
characters.name: Wolf

characters.description: Cinder's android friend, at last in an escort-droid body of her own and delighted by it. She joins the crew on the ground rather than staying with the ship.
characters.name: Iko

characters.description: Emperor of the Eastern Commonwealth, arriving on Luna to be married to Levana in a ceremony that will make her empress of his country. He knows Cinder is coming, cannot show that he knows, and has to play the compliant bridegroom in a palace where any Lunar in the room can read a slip.
characters.name: Emperor Kai

characters.description: The Eastern Commonwealth's royal advisor, who has come to Luna with Kai and is one of very few Earthens in a palace full of people who can make him believe anything.
characters.name: Konn Torin

characters.description: Levana's head thaumaturge, returned from Earth with a captive, a failure to explain and a guard she no longer trusts.
characters.name: Sybil Mira

characters.description: One of Levana's senior thaumaturges and a fixture of her court, smooth, attentive and unpleasant in a way that never quite breaks etiquette. The queen has decided that he will marry Winter.
characters.name: Aimery Park

characters.description: Wolf's mother, still living in the outer sector her sons were taken from, who has spent years being told what happened to them and believing none of it.
characters.name: Maha Kesley

characters.description: Wolf's younger brother, who stayed in Levana's army after Paris and has been through everything the programme does to a soldier who does not run.
characters.name: Ran Kesley

characters.description: The Lunar defector and scientist, who came to the moon ahead of the crew to look for the shell children Levana keeps for their blood, and for the daughter who was taken from him among them.
characters.name: Dr. Dmitri Erland

recaps.ending: Levana marries Kai, and the marriage buys her nothing. Cress breaks into Luna's broadcast network and puts Levana's unglamoured face - burned and scarred since childhood - in front of the entire moon, destroying the illusion her rule was built on, and Cinder declares herself publicly as Princess Selene. The outer sectors rise, the fighting reaches Artemisia, and Cinder faces Levana in the palace and kills her. Winter, whom Levana had ordered killed and Jacin saved by faking her death, survives and is at Scarlet's side through the revolt. Dr. Erland dies on Luna, and Cress learns before the end that he was her father. Cinder is crowned Queen Selene of Luna, immediately releases the plague antidote to Earth without conditions, frees the shell children Levana had kept in captivity as its source, and dissolves the aristocracy's hold on the sectors. Then she abdicates: rather than hold a throne she never wanted, she puts Luna's future to an elected government and leaves the crown behind. Kai's marriage to Levana ends with Levana, and he and Cinder are free to be together. Scarlet and Wolf return to the farm in France, Cress and Thorne take the Rampion out to help distribute the antidote across Earth, and Winter and Jacin stay on Luna to help rebuild it.
recaps.in_short: Cinder's crew lands on Luna to overthrow Queen Levana during her wedding to Emperor Kai. On the moon they find Scarlet caged in the royal menagerie and Princess Winter, Levana's stepdaughter, loved by the people and slowly unravelling from the sickness that comes of refusing to use her Lunar gift. Levana orders Winter killed; her guard Jacin fakes the death instead, and Winter and Scarlet escape into the outer sectors. Cinder raises the mining and manufacturing districts against the capital while Cress works to break Levana's grip on what the Lunar people are allowed to see. The wedding goes ahead, Cinder is captured and reveals herself publicly as Princess Selene, Wolf is taken and forcibly remade by Levana's surgeons, and Erland dies on Luna after Cress learns he was her father. Cress finally broadcasts Levana's true, scarred face across the moon, the revolt reaches Artemisia, and Cinder kills Levana in the palace. Crowned Queen Selene, she releases the antidote to Earth, frees the captive shells, and then abdicates so that Luna can elect its own government.

recaps.text: Previously: Linh Cinder, a cyborg mechanic on Earth, discovered she was Lunar and then that she is Princess Selene, the heir Queen Levana tried to have burned as a small child. She escaped prison with the thief Carswell Thorne, took up with the French farmer Scarlet Benoit and the defected Lunar soldier Wolf, and rescued Cress, a Lunar shell imprisoned for seven years in an orbiting satellite as Levana's hacker and spy. The rescue cost them: Scarlet was captured and shipped to Luna as a curiosity for the royal menagerie, and Cress and Thorne crashed into the Sahara. Dr. Erland, the Lunar defector who first told Cinder what she was, revealed that the letumosis plague was engineered on Luna as a weapon and that its antidote is drawn from captive shell children, one of whom was his own stolen daughter, and left for the moon to find her. He never realised it was Cress. Cinder's crew abducted Emperor Kai from his wedding procession and told him everything; Kai chose to go through with the marriage on Luna anyway, because the ceremony is the one thing that will open Levana's palace. Kai has gone ahead to be married. Cinder has followed, meaning to raise Luna's outer sectors and take the throne she was born to.

On Luna, Princess Winter lives in her stepmother's palace as its most beloved ornament. She has refused since childhood to use her Lunar gift to manipulate anyone, and pays for it: she hallucinates constantly, and the court has settled comfortably on the idea that she is mad. Her childhood friend Jacin Clay returns from Earth in disgrace, having lost the thaumaturge he was guarding, and Winter intervenes at his trial to keep him alive; Levana assigns him to Winter as her personal guard. In the royal menagerie Winter visits Scarlet Benoit, held as an exhibit and missing a finger taken as an example, and finds her rude, unfrightened and the best company she has had in years.

Levana's court prepares for the royal wedding, with Earth's emperor arriving to be married on Luna. The queen announces that Winter will marry her thaumaturge Aimery Park, which Winter refuses as far as anyone in that palace is able to refuse anything. Levana has begun to understand what her stepdaughter is: a young woman the Lunar people love, in a court where she herself is only obeyed, and she does not intend to live alongside that indefinitely. Above the moon, the Rampion approaches with Cinder, Thorne, Cress, Wolf and Iko aboard, and no way through Luna's defences that does not involve being shot down.

The crew gets down to the lunar surface and into the outer sectors, the mining and manufacturing districts whose workers keep Artemisia in luxury and are worked to death doing it. Cinder's plan is a revolution rather than an assassination: convince the sectors that Princess Selene is alive and standing in front of them, and bring them to the capital while the wedding has the palace open. It goes slowly. The sectors have been punished for less, most people take her for a lunatic or a trap, and every hour spent persuading one district is an hour Levana's guards have to find them. In Artemisia, Levana settles the question of her stepdaughter: Winter is to be killed, quietly and by someone close enough to get near her.

Wolf's own sector is one of the districts the crew reaches, and he sees his mother and his brother again; neither reunion goes the way he had let himself imagine. Cinder wins over her first sectors and starts a chain of them. In Artemisia, Cress works on Luna's tightly controlled communications, hunting a way to speak to the whole moon at once - the only way to beat a queen whose power depends on nobody being allowed to see clearly. Kai arrives for the wedding, plays the compliant bridegroom in a palace where every courtier can read a flinch, and waits.

Levana's order against Winter is carried out at court: the princess is poisoned in front of witnesses and pronounced dead. Jacin, who was given the job, chose a poison he could reverse and revives her afterwards, and the two of them get Scarlet out of the menagerie. Winter, Jacin and Scarlet escape Artemisia into the outer sectors, where the story that the princess has been murdered by her stepmother is already spreading faster than the truth. Winter, who has never been permitted to be anything but decorative, discovers that the sectors will listen to her.

The revolt gathers. Sector after sector joins, Winter's survival becomes the proof that Levana kills her own family, and Scarlet and Winter travel together raising districts while Cinder moves toward the capital. Levana's thaumaturges are sent out to break the uprising, and the fighting is one-sided and brutal. Cinder is captured before she can reach the wedding and taken into the palace, and the royal ceremony goes ahead with Earth's emperor and Luna's queen married in front of the court.

In the palace Cinder declares herself openly as Princess Selene, in front of the court, the Earthen delegation and Luna's cameras, and Levana can no longer pretend the girl is only an escaped cyborg. Levana is now legally empress of the Eastern Commonwealth by marriage. Wolf is taken by the queen's people and handed to her surgeons, who put him through the operation the special operatives programme reserves for its most useful soldiers, and he comes out of it changed and barely his own. Beneath the city, Cress and Thorne search the tunnels for a way into Luna's central network, and find Dr. Erland, who came to the moon looking for the captive shell children and his own lost daughter.

Erland dies on Luna, and Cress learns what he never worked out on Earth: she was the daughter he had been searching for since she was taken as an infant. Then she does the thing she came to do. Cress breaks into Luna's broadcast network and puts the queen in front of her own people without her glamour, so that the entire moon sees the burned and scarred face Levana has spent her life hiding behind an illusion. The court, the sectors and the Earthen delegation all see it together, and the fear that held Luna in place breaks with it.

The uprising reaches Artemisia. The outer sectors march on the capital, the palace guard and the thaumaturges fight them through the domes and the corridors, and the wedding party becomes a battlefield. Cinder frees herself and fights her way inward, Winter and Scarlet come in with the sectors, Jacin holds the line around Winter, and Thorne and Iko fight through the palace with them. Wolf, remade and half-lost, is brought back to himself by Scarlet. Levana, exposed and losing, falls back on the one thing she has left, which is her own gift, and the last of the fighting closes around the throne room.

Cinder faces Levana in the palace and kills her. With the queen dead, the marriage that made her empress of the Eastern Commonwealth ends with her, and Kai is free. Cinder is crowned Queen Selene of Luna. Her first acts are to release the letumosis antidote to Earth without conditions and to free the shell children Levana had kept alive in captivity as its source, Cress's own kind, held in tanks beneath the city for years.

Cinder does not keep the throne. Having taken it to end Levana, she uses it to dismantle what Levana built - the aristocracy's grip on the outer sectors, the surveillance, the special operatives programme - and then abdicates, putting Luna's future to an elected government rather than another queen. Earth and Luna begin negotiating as neighbours rather than enemies, with the plague finally treatable everywhere. Winter and Jacin stay on Luna to help rebuild it, Winter still refusing to use the gift that is slowly costing her. Scarlet and Wolf go back to the farm in France. Cress and Thorne take the Rampion out to run antidote to the places on Earth that still have none, with Iko aboard. Kai and Cinder, an emperor and a girl who has just given away a crown, are left with the ordinary problem of what they are to each other now that nothing is stopping them.

characters.description: The Earth-born proprietor of the Wandering Inn, known for extending friendship across the divisions surrounding Liscor. Her inn has become a refuge for people who rarely find acceptance elsewhere.
characters.name: Erin

characters.description: A classless runner from Earth and one of Erin's friends. She travels with the Frost Faerie Ivolethe and approaches unfamiliar powers, secret knowledge, and dangerous commissions with persistent caution.
characters.name: Ryoka

characters.description: Erin's barmaid and the person entrusted with the Wandering Inn when Erin is absent. She is building a life through the inn's daily work and its unusual community.
characters.name: Lyonette

characters.description: The young chieftain of the Flooded Waters tribe and an established battlefield leader.
characters.name: Rags

characters.description: Leader of the Redfang tribe and its elite warriors. Though Rags defeated him before this campaign, he retains independent command and commands more personal loyalty within their coalition.
characters.name: Garen Redfang

aliases: Great Chieftain of the Mountain City Tribe
characters.description: The immense Great Chieftain of a powerful northern Goblin tribe. He offers an alliance that commits his mountain only if the Goblin Lord attacks it, and he treats Rags' authority with open contempt.
characters.name: Tremborag

characters.description: A Hobgoblin chieftain whose loyalty to Rags is visible even within Tremborag's territory. He remains close enough to act as one of her guards when much of the coalition's support wavers.
characters.name: Goldstone Chieftain

characters.description: The orphaned last survivor of the Stone Spears tribe, now sheltered at the Wandering Inn under Lyonette's care. Trauma and fear surrounding her white fur leave her convinced that disaster follows her.
characters.name: The young white-furred Gnoll

characters.description: A sword-bearing skeleton that pursues the young Gnoll to a dungeon fissure, then pauses when she is left hanging above the drop.
characters.name: Toren

characters.description: A Drake general who helped defend the young Gnoll during the destruction of her tribe. At the inn he supports Lyonette and takes an active role when the child needs rescue.
characters.name: Zel

characters.description: A powerful Azure Antinium who joins the effort to recover the young Gnoll from the dungeon. Her magic enables the rescuers to descend into the fissure and return to the surface.
characters.name: Xrn

characters.description: Tremborag's chief shaman and a practitioner of magic drawn from the strength of a tribe. She presents herself to Rags as a potential ally and claims power far beyond the mountain's lesser shamans.
characters.name: Ulvama

characters.description: The former Goldstone Chieftain, newly named by Rags. His conduct in Tremborag's restricted quarter proves protective rather than exploitative, and he will refuse commands that violate his understanding of what Goblins should be.
characters.name: Pyrite

characters.description: A Redfang Warrior who speaks for the contingent that followed Rags out of the mountain. He presses her to devise a practical defense against cavalry, one of the tribe's most dangerous battlefield threats.
characters.name: Red Scar

characters.description: Ryoka's mysterious client, appearing as a white-bearded stranger with overwhelming command of basic magic. He seeks Erin's help understanding an artifact from Earth after easily defeating the Horns.
characters.name: Teriarch

characters.description: An elderly Hobgoblin who hides the extent of his intelligence. His personal memories reach back to earlier Goblin Kings, giving Rags evidence of a past in which Goblins formed peaceful alliances with other peoples.
characters.name: Greybeard

characters.description: A Goblin commander who leads a separate group within Rags' enlarged tribe. She challenges Rags' decision to require regular training because it conflicts with Goblin custom.
characters.name: Poison Bite

characters.description: A half-Elf adventurer and ice mage who belongs to the Horns of Hammerad.
characters.name: Ceria

characters.description: A mage of the Horns of Hammerad whose unusual command of undead magic sets him apart.
characters.name: Pisces

characters.description: A true stone construct charged with preserving Wistrom and enforcing its rules. She warns new arrivals about the academy's restricted places, dangerous experiments, and golems.
characters.name: Cognita

characters.description: A severe Wistrom instructor who criticizes Ceria's spell construction and refuses ordinary access to combat teaching. Her challenges demand resourcefulness as well as magical strength.
characters.name: The ice mage

characters.description: The frontline fighter of the re-formed Horns of Hammerad. She travels with Ceria, Pisces, and Ksmvr as the team makes its way back toward Liscor.
characters.name: Yvlon Byres

characters.description: An Antinium fighter and member of the Horns of Hammerad. His place in the adventuring team brings him into Erin's growing circle of people from different species.
characters.name: Ksmvr

characters.description: An alchemist who collaborates with Erin on practical inventions.
characters.name: Octavia

characters.description: A senior Antinium of the Liscor Hive and one of Erin's friends. His responsibilities to the Hive coexist uneasily with the individual relationships he has formed around the inn.
characters.name: Klbkch

characters.description: An individual Antinium associated with Erin and the Wandering Inn. He has begun developing a life and responsibilities beyond the role ordinarily assigned to a worker.
characters.name: Pawn

characters.description: A Drake strategist and chess player within Erin's established circle in Liscor.
characters.name: Olesm

characters.description: An Antinium sub-leader who directs workers alongside Anand during Esthelm's reconstruction. The pair coordinate the force without spoken orders.
characters.name: Belgrade

characters.description: An Antinium sub-leader who shares responsibility with Belgrade for directing the workers sent to rebuild Esthelm. The two can coordinate their forces mind-to-mind.
characters.name: Anand

characters.description: A visiting Antinium Progenitor from another Hive. Tersk accompanies Xrn to Esthelm as an observer of Liscor's increasingly individual Antinium and their relief mission.
characters.name: Tersk

characters.description: A blind man devoted to protecting River Farm and to Durene, his half-troll companion. He has established authority over the village while adapting to a world he cannot see.
characters.name: Laken

characters.description: Laken's half-troll guide and protective companion. She helps him navigate the world and remains central to his efforts to secure River Farm.
characters.name: Durene

characters.description: A Frost Faerie who travels with Ryoka. She serves as a guide to powers and dangers that mortal knowledge does not readily explain.
characters.name: Ivolethe

characters.description: The head of the Reinhart household, whose protection gives Ryoka shelter and access while placing her movements under the household's supervision.
characters.name: Magnolia Reinhart

characters.description: Magnolia Reinhart's butler and Ryoka's assigned guide in Invercil. His service gives Ryoka privileged access while also tying her movements to Magnolia Reinhart's household.
characters.name: Reynold

characters.description: A runner whose unexpected absence from his usual delivery circuit prompts concern at the Invercil Runners' Guild. Ryoka asks the guild to investigate where he has gone.
characters.name: Valceif Godfrey

characters.description: A blue fledgling being raised by Laken and Durene. Caring for the young bird has given Laken a new class connected to handling animals.
characters.name: Frostwing

characters.description: A caller who reaches Ryoka through her phone and claims to be an Earth arrival seeking others like himself. Ryoka and Laken cannot verify his identity or whether his connection to Wistrom is safe.
characters.name: The Wistrom caller

characters.description: Klbkch's partner in an improvised Christmas mission. He helps distribute presents and stop burglars, then privately exchanges a gift with Klbkch after learning that Santa is fictional.
characters.name: Klbkch's Christmas partner

characters.description: A surviving Antinium Progenitor identified as the one who killed Zel's mentor.
characters.name: The Deathless

recaps.ending: River Farm survives its immediate shortage after Ryoka delivers supplies through the blizzard, and Laken remains responsible for its recovery. Erin's magical inn has become a center for travel, relief, and cross-species cooperation, but Christmas leaves her friends aware of how desperately she misses Earth. Lyonette resolves to help, without yet knowing how. Ceria and Pisces remain with the Horns, recognized by Cognita as Wistrom graduates but divided by Pisces' necromancy and exile. Rags continues south with an independent tribe while Tremborag pursues her and the Goblin Lord's larger force remains ahead. Xrn's private purpose, the Deathless, and a secret message to a northern lord leave wider conflicts unresolved. Ryoka and Laken maintain a cautious alliance as Earth arrivals and distrust the caller from Wistrom. During the solstice, Erin refuses to trade her soul and retains a white-silver coin. Ryoka rejects the entities' false restoration of her missing fingers, burns both the fingers and her altered scarf, and escapes with Ivolethe. The beings and Ryoka's luminous rescuers remain unidentified.
recaps.in_short: Rags rejects Tremborag's mountain, frees its captives, and leads a newly disciplined Goblin tribe south toward the greater war. Ceria and Pisces' Wistrom past ends with both recognized as mages, but Pisces is exiled and their friendship is broken. Erin returns to a thriving inn, becomes a Magical Innkeeper, and uses its portal and alliances to relieve Esthelm. Ryoka meets Laken, another person from Earth, helps equip the Horns, and carries emergency supplies to River Farm. Christmas exposes Erin's longing for home while hidden Antinium history surfaces. On the winter solstice, strange visitors offer Erin treasures for her soul and hostile beings offer Ryoka the restoration of her lost fingers. Both refuse. Erin is left with an unnatural coin, while Ryoka destroys the offered fingers and escapes with Ivolethe, still injured.
