recaps.text: Previously: Erin, an innkeeper from Earth, built the Wandering Inn outside Liscor into a refuge shared by adventurers, Antinium, Drakes, Gnolls, and other outsiders. Ryoka, another arrival from Earth, remained classless and pursued dangerous running work with the Frost Faerie Ivolethe. The Horns of Hammerad re-formed around Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon, and Ksmvr after surviving the ruins of Albez. Their recovered artifacts and Erin's portal door opened new possibilities, but also created risks. Rags emerged as a young Goblin leader while a Goblin Lord's armies devastated settlements including Esthelm. Laken established authority at River Farm with Durene beside him. Lyonette remained at Erin's inn and began taking responsibility for the young white-furred survivor of the Stone Spears tribe. The dungeon beneath Liscor, conflict among the Antinium, and the presence of multiple people from Earth all remained unresolved.

Rags leads a Goblin coalition north after learning that the army she defeated was only one part of the Goblin Lord's much larger force. At Tremborag's mountain, Garen Redfang negotiates a limited alliance that leaves Rags politically diminished. She discovers that the prosperous settlement rests on hierarchy, coercion, and imprisoned human women. The Goldstone Chieftain proves that his visits to the captives were meant to protect them, and Rags names him Pyrite. Rejecting Tremborag's rule, she leads a revolt, empties his armory, and escapes with supplies, followers, and hundreds of freed captives. After delivering the women to a human city, she establishes a forest camp and begins training mobile pike formations against cavalry. At the Wandering Inn, the traumatized young Gnoll falls into the dungeon while fleeing accusations tied to her white fur. Lyonette organizes a rescue with Zel, Ksmvr, Xrn, and others. The child survives and accepts the inn as home.

Erin finances Octavia's experiments and uses the portal door to support the traveling Horns, while refusing demands to turn the limited, mana-hungry connection into a public delivery service. A white-bearded stranger named Teriarch intercepts the Horns, overwhelms them with basic spells, and questions Erin about Ryoka's copied phone. He teaches Ceria and Pisces how to turn simple magic and the surrounding snow into a storm, then departs. His human appearance is a remote guise controlled by a dragon. Rags reorganizes her enlarged tribe and assigns the Redfang Warriors as a mobile vanguard. Costly encounters with monsters and undead expose the limits of her command, but Greybeard's memories show that Goblins once maintained peace with other peoples. Rags adopts regular training, rescues another tribe, and captures caravan supplies without killing the travelers. She turns south with a doctrine based on discipline and lower casualties. Ceria's history then begins: as a prospective student, she meets Pisces on the voyage to Wistrom, and the pair enter the dangerous academy together.

At Wistrom, Ceria and Pisces survive harassment, factional maneuvering, and an entrance examination by sharing knowledge and protecting each other. They secretly acquire a warded spellbook with Cognita's rule-bound assistance. Pisces masters Flashstep, while Ceria solves an ice mage's barrier test through practical ingenuity. Their friendship breaks after a pirate ambush, when Pisces raises the dead to protect survivors and is publicly exposed as a necromancer. Wistrom strips his support, but the ice mage accepts Ceria as her apprentice. Years later, Ceria's master and four senior mages challenge Cognita and the other guardian golems for access to Wistrom's sealed upper levels. All five challengers die. Pisces reanimates their bodies to enter the catacombs and steals bones from an archmage's tomb, releasing shades that kill nearly sixty people. Cognita prevents his execution, and he receives permanent exile. Ceria condemns the academy's inaction. Cognita publicly recognizes both Ceria and Pisces as full mages, but they leave Wistrom separately, their friendship shattered.

The Horns travel back toward Liscor with Erin, passing through damaged Esthelm and learning that Yvlon's gold-rank brother helped defend the city before leaving to search for her. Erin brings blankets and food, but Esthelm remains short of supplies and vulnerable. At the Wandering Inn, Lyonette has kept the business running, cared for the young Gnoll, and filled the rooms with two gold-rank teams. Erin initially overlooks that achievement, then accepts Zel's rebuke and apologizes. She reveals the portal door connecting the inn to Octavia's shop, although its mana reserve is small enough to strand travelers and its closing edge is dangerous. After the inn fills with guests from many species, Erin reaches level thirty and becomes a Magical Innkeeper. The building gains a rich magical reserve and preservation magic. Wanting to help beyond her immediate friends, Erin organizes a relief expedition to Esthelm. Adventurers, Liscor's people, and hundreds of Antinium join. Pawn commands the Antinium contingent, Belgrade and Anand direct reconstruction, and Zel begins teaching Pawn how a leader can comfort dying soldiers.

The mixed relief mission supplies and repairs Esthelm, demonstrating practical cooperation among Antinium, Drakes, Gnolls, humans, and adventurers despite enduring distrust. Meanwhile, Ryoka researches ancient threats while staying under Magnolia Reinhart's protection and surveillance. In Invercil she notices Laken and Durene after adventurers harass Durene for being half-troll. Laken's German speech leads Ryoka to suspect the truth, and they confirm that both came from Earth. Laken is an Emperor seeking help for avalanche-stricken River Farm. He purchases provisions, wagons, livestock, tools, escorts, and winter protection, using his authority without openly declaring his class. Ryoka has the Horns' recovered artifacts appraised and learns that their ancient wand is exceptionally valuable. She also learns that runner Valceif Godfrey was killed by bandits using a sleep spell. Though she blames herself because he had given her his protective charm, another runner places responsibility on the killers. Ryoka warns Laken to conceal his phone and continues her work while Magnolia Reinhart's agents track her.

Back in Liscor, Erin attempts to save a Gnoll warrior's infected hand using cleaning, salt water, honey, and clean dressings suggested by Ryoka, while acknowledging that amputation may still be necessary. She plans a Christmas gathering and hires Octavia to investigate inexpensive matches and medicinal mold. The inn's visitors adopt Go, and Belgrade receives strategic encouragement from Zel. Ryoka and Laken form a guarded alliance based on their shared Earth origin. A caller linked to Wistrom contacts Ryoka's phone and claims to be gathering people from Earth, but neither runner nor Emperor trusts him with their location. Ryoka sells the Horns' ancient wand for equipment, magical items, and coin for the team. When a blizzard threatens River Farm before Laken's wagons can arrive, Ryoka carries emergency provisions through the storm. Ivolethe and other Frost Faeries guide her to the village. Ryoka delivers food, blankets, tools, and presents, comforts children grieving losses from the avalanche, and leaves River Farm able to survive the immediate crisis.

Erin holds Christmas at the Wandering Inn, but singing about home exposes her grief and forces her guests to recognize how much she wants to return to Earth. Zel and Klbkch nearly fight over the Antinium Wars until Xrn intervenes. She identifies herself as the Small Queen and says another surviving Progenitor, the Deathless, killed Zel's mentor. Xrn then takes Klbkch aside for undisclosed business, while Pisces discovers that a Griffin Hunt mage has secretly contacted a northern lord. Lyonette sees Erin crying alone and resolves to do something for her. On the winter solstice, Ryoka leaves River Farm and becomes trapped in a supernatural storm. Three inhuman beings at a fire offer alluring paths and restore her missing fingers, but she refuses them and escapes with help from unidentified lights. She burns the moving fingers and an altered scarf, remaining injured. At the same time, Erin welcomes three strange men into the inn. They consume its food and offer powerful treasures for her soul. Erin refuses every bargain. The visitors leave a white-silver coin behind, giving her physical proof of the encounter. The solstice ends with both women alive, but the entities and their purposes remain unknown.

characters.description: Queen of Monsea in her twenties, years into the work of repairing what her father did to her kingdom, and tired of it. Precise, stubborn and better at arithmetic than at diplomacy, she refuses to accept the comfortable explanation of anything. When two of her envoys drown on the far side of the world, she declines to call it an accident and goes to find out herself.
characters.name: Bitterblue

characters.description: An enormous, ancient creature that lives at the bottom of the bay off Winterkeep's capital, alone with a hoard of things that have sunk to it over centuries. It thinks in long, slow loops, worries about its treasures, and watches a Monsean ship come down through the water at the start of the book.
characters.name: The Keeper

characters.description: A Middluns-born lord and a leader of the Council, long since stripped of his estate for it, now Bitterblue's closest ally and the person she most trusts to tell her when she is wrong. Steady, courteous, deeply competent, and careful to keep his feelings for the queen to himself.
characters.name: Giddon

characters.description: Bitterblue's half-sister and her spy, Graced with hiding: she can hold still and let an onlooker's eye take her for a crate, a rock, a piece of the ship. She keeps her relationship to the queen private, prefers being unseen to being included, and is happier working alone than being anybody's family.
characters.name: Hava

characters.description: A student at Winterkeep's academy, daughter of one of the country's most powerful political families, sharp-eyed and careful about what she lets people see. She keeps her grades up, keeps her relationships casual, and keeps out of her mother's way, and she has begun paying attention to the people who come and go from her family's houses.
characters.name: Lovisa Cavenda

characters.description: Lovisa's father, a wealthy and charming member of Winterkeep's parliament on the Industrialist side, warm with his children in a way his wife is not, and involved in every important conversation in the country.
characters.name: Benni Cavenda

characters.description: Lovisa's mother, a Scholar politician of considerable power, cold, exacting and physically controlling with her daughter. She runs her household as an instrument and expects it to perform.
characters.name: Ferla Cavenda

characters.description: Lovisa's uncle, an adventurer who travels the world rather than sit in Winterkeep's politics, and the one member of her family Lovisa has ever liked. He has gone missing on his travels, which everyone finds unremarkable and Lovisa does not.
characters.name: Katu Cavenda

characters.description: A veterinary student at the academy, from a working family rather than a political one, blunt about what she thinks of the rich. She patches up injured animals, including the blue foxes people bond with, and she has known Lovisa long enough not to be impressed by her.
characters.name: Nev

characters.description: A professor at the academy, wealthy, distracted and eccentric, who keeps an unusual number of blue foxes in her house and takes an unusual amount of interest in her students.
characters.name: Quona Varana

recaps.ending: The envoys' deaths were murder, arranged to protect a secret zilfium project, and the plot ran through the Cavenda family. Lovisa is the one who assembles the proof and acts on it, against both her parents, and it costs her the household she grew up in: the family's power collapses, and she is left responsible for her three younger brothers and free of her mother for the first time. Bitterblue, given up for drowned by everyone including Giddon and Hava, is alive, and is found and got free. Her reappearance ends the diplomatic fiction that Monsea was being told the truth about anything in Winterkeep. Bitterblue and Giddon, each having spent part of the book believing the other lost, stop pretending about what they are to each other and end the book together, openly. Bitterblue sails home to Monsea with Giddon, Hava and the knowledge of what Winterkeep's industrial politics is capable of, and Winterkeep's argument about whether to burn zilfium at all is left unresolved and now far more dangerous. The great creature at the bottom of the bay, and the fact that both the silbercows and the bonded foxes have long known things about their humans that their humans do not know about them, remain part of the world the story leaves open.
recaps.in_short: Two Monsean envoys drown when their ship sinks in Winterkeep's bay, and Queen Bitterblue refuses to accept it as an accident: they had been investigating zilfium, the fuel at the centre of Winterkeep's politics. She sails there with Giddon and her half-sister and spy Hava, and gets nothing but polite obstruction. Meanwhile Lovisa Cavenda, a student and the daughter of two of Winterkeep's most powerful politicians, starts noticing what her parents are hiding at the family's northern estate. Bitterblue's boat goes down in the bay and she is presumed dead; she is in fact alive, taken and held prisoner in the north, while Giddon and Hava grieve and keep digging. Lovisa uncovers the truth - that her father arranged the envoys' deaths to protect a secret weapon project, with her mother implicated - and it is Lovisa who finds and frees the queen. The Cavendas' power collapses, Lovisa is left to raise her younger brothers on her own terms, and Bitterblue and Giddon return to Monsea together, no longer pretending about each other.

recaps.text: Previously: Bitterblue became queen of Monsea at ten, after her father King Leck, whose Grace let him make anyone believe anything he said, was killed at the end of a thirty-five-year reign of hidden atrocities. As a young woman she uncovered what he had actually done, discovered that her own advisers had been his instruments, and set her kingdom to collecting and telling its true history instead of burying it. She learned in the process that she has a half-sister, Hava, Leck's other daughter, who is Graced with hiding herself and now works as her spy. Her allies include Giddon of the Council, the organisation that works against bad kings across the seven kingdoms. The seven kingdoms have also stopped being the whole world: a route east opened to the Dells, and Monsea now trades across the sea with the continent of Torla, whose leading nation, Winterkeep, is a democracy far ahead of the seven kingdoms technologically. This book opens years later, with Monsean envoys stationed there.

A Monsean ship goes down in the bay off Winterkeep's capital, drowning two of Queen Bitterblue's envoys, and an enormous, solitary creature on the sea floor watches the wreck settle into the trove of sunken things it has been guarding for centuries. In Monsea, Bitterblue refuses the official account. Her envoys had been asking questions about zilfium, the fuel that dominates Winterkeep's politics, and had written home about something they had found. She sails for Winterkeep with Giddon and her half-sister Hava, whose Grace lets her go about unnoticed. In Winterkeep itself, Lovisa Cavenda, an academy student and the daughter of two of the country's most powerful politicians, is watching the guests who come and go from her family's houses and beginning to understand that she does not know what her parents are doing.

Winterkeep is a democracy split between two parties: Scholars, who argue that zilfium should stay in the ground, and Industrialists, who want it burned to power a modern nation. Lovisa's mother Ferla is a Scholar of considerable power and her father Benni is an Industrialist, and the household is a political instrument as much as a family. Bitterblue's questions in the capital get courtesy and no facts, and she chafes at being handled; she and Giddon grow closer as the delegation gets nowhere. The country is stranger than Monsea's envoys reported: blue foxes bond to human households and touch their minds, and telepathic sea creatures called silbercows carry pictures of what they have seen to anyone who will swim out and listen - including pictures of a ship going down. Lovisa's uncle Katu has gone missing on his travels, and her father's northern estate is receiving visitors it should not be receiving.

Bitterblue is lost on the water. Her boat goes down in the bay and everyone, Giddon and Hava included, believes the queen of Monsea has drowned exactly as her envoys did. She has not: she is alive, taken out of the water by people who wanted her gone, and held prisoner far to the north where nobody will look for her. In the capital, Giddon and Hava grieve and go on working the diplomatic and criminal trail, now with a dead monarch on their hands and a delegation that cannot say what it suspects. Lovisa, following her own family rather than the politics, gets close enough to the northern house to see that whatever her father is protecting there is worth killing foreign envoys over, and close enough for it to cost her the safety of being an obedient daughter.

Lovisa assembles it: the Monsean envoys were murdered because they had learned that her father was secretly funding work toward a zilfium weapon, and her mother's hands are not clean either. She is now the only person in a position to prove it, acting against both her parents, with three young brothers to think about and no adult ally she can safely rely on. Bitterblue, still held and still believed drowned, has worked out roughly the same thing from the other end, and has to keep herself alive long enough for it to matter. Giddon and Hava, meanwhile, are pursuing the same trail in the capital in the belief that they are avenging a dead queen rather than looking for a living one.

Bitterblue is found alive and freed, and Lovisa is the one who does it, acting on what she has learned about her own family. The Cavendas' scheme is exposed and their power destroyed. Lovisa comes out of it responsible for her younger brothers and, for the first time, out from under her mother, choosing a life she picks rather than one arranged for her. Bitterblue, alive after being mourned, ends the diplomatic pretence with Winterkeep and prepares to take Monsea home a much clearer picture of what an industrial power will do to protect a weapon. She and Giddon, each of whom spent part of the book believing the other lost, stop pretending about each other and are together openly. Winterkeep's own argument over whether to burn zilfium is unresolved and now considerably more dangerous, and the creature on the floor of the bay keeps its hoard, its solitude, and the secrets that the silbercows and the bonded foxes have been keeping from the humans they live among.

characters.description: A young man from the isolated Two Rivers who has been proclaimed the Dragon Reborn, the prophesied champion fated to face the Dark One at the Last Battle and to break the world in the doing. He wields the male half of the One Power, saidin, which carries the Dark One's taint and slowly maddens any man who touches it. Hunted, used, and feared, he has bound the Aiel to him as their foretold leader, seized thrones across the land, killed several of the Forsaken, and raised an army of male channelers, all while trusting almost no one and hardening himself against the losses around him.
characters.name: Rand al'Thor

characters.description: A former gambler and rogue from the Two Rivers, quick with dice, luck, and excuses, and reluctantly one of the most important men alive. Ta'veren like his boyhood friend Rand, he carries the memories of long-dead generals in his head, wears a foxhead medallion that turns aside the One Power, and once sounded the legendary Horn of Valere. He commands the Band of the Red Hand, a growing army, though he would rather be anywhere but at the center of great events. He was last caught in the chaos of a Seanchan assault on the city of Ebou Dar.
characters.name: Mat Cauthon

characters.description: A broad-shouldered blacksmith from the Two Rivers who can speak with wolves and see through their eyes, a gift he distrusts and tries to hide. Steady, deliberate, and quietly powerful, he has become a battle leader almost against his will, given a lordship and a following. He is devoted to his wife, Faile, and as this book opens he is consumed by a single purpose: to recover her after she was seized by the renegade Shaido Aiel.
characters.name: Perrin Aybara

characters.description: An innkeeper's daughter from the Two Rivers who has risen with astonishing speed to become a powerful channeler and the chosen Amyrlin Seat of the Aes Sedai who broke with the White Tower. Young for the role and underestimated by the sisters who raised her thinking to control her, she is disciplined, clever, and far more formidable than she appears. She leads the rebel army besieging the city of Tar Valon, determined to unseat the usurping Amyrlin and heal the Tower's division.
characters.name: Egwene al'Vere

characters.description: The former Wisdom of Emond's Field, fierce, stubborn, and protective of the young people she once looked after in the Two Rivers. A gifted Healer whose power long depended on her temper, she has become an Aes Sedai and married Lan, the Dragon Reborn's onetime protector. Blunt to the point of rudeness and impatient with fools, she stands among the few willing to challenge Rand to his face.
characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara

characters.description: The Daughter-Heir of Andor and a newly raised Aes Sedai, trained in the One Power and determined to claim her late mother's Lion Throne. Proud, principled, and politically astute, she is one of the women Rand loves and is bound to him. She works with the female channelers gathered around her to secure Caemlyn and the crown that is hers by right.
characters.name: Elayne Trakand

characters.description: A sharp-tongued young woman who sees images and auras around people that reveal glimpses of their futures, a talent she cannot control but has never known to fail. Practical and loyal, she has attached herself to Rand as one of the three women fated to love him, and she stays close as adviser and companion, reading the dangers gathering around him.
characters.name: Min Farshaw

characters.description: A fierce young Aiel woman training to become a Wise One, one of the channelers among her people. Raised as a warrior before setting her spears aside, she is proud, honest to a fault, and bound by the strict customs of the Aiel. She is one of the three women tied to Rand by love and prophecy, though duty and her people's ways complicate what lies between them.
characters.name: Aviendha

characters.description: A legendary Aes Sedai of fearsome reputation, thought long dead, who has come out of retirement to involve herself in the Dragon Reborn's affairs. Famous for handling men who can channel, she is imperious, secretive, and utterly certain of her own judgement, intent on teaching Rand and the male channelers around him something she believes they must learn before the Last Battle.
characters.name: Cadsuane Melaidhrin

characters.description: Perrin's wife, a small, sharp-featured noblewoman of Saldaea with a hunter's boldness and a temper to match. Proud and strong-willed, she meets her husband's steadiness with fire. As this book begins she is a captive of the Shaido Aiel, held far from Perrin, who will stop at nothing to find her.
characters.name: Faile Bashere

characters.description: A small, imperious young woman of the Seanchan, the empire whose forces have invaded the mainland from across the ocean. Heir to the Crystal Throne and known by the title Daughter of the Nine Moons, she is composed, watchful, and dangerous, schooled from birth in a ruthless court where those who channel are collared as slaves. Prophecy has long foretold that Mat Cauthon would meet and marry the Daughter of the Nine Moons.
characters.name: Tuon

recaps.ending: Winter's Heart ends with two turning points. Mat Cauthon breaks out of Seanchan-held Ebou Dar and flees north, taking with him Tuon, the Daughter of the Nine Moons and heir to the Seanchan empire, beginning the strange courtship prophecy demands of them. Far away, at the cursed ruins of Shadar Logoth, Rand al'Thor accomplishes what every Aes Sedai believed impossible. Using the great sa'angreal Choedan Kal, and linked through Nynaeve and Cadsuane's circle, he pits the tainted male Power against the ancient evil of the dead city and cleanses saidin of the Dark One's corruption. The Forsaken who come to stop him are driven off, and for the first time since the Breaking of the World men can channel without the certainty of madness, though few yet believe it has truly happened. Elayne consolidates her position in Caemlyn as she pursues the Lion Throne, and Perrin, still without Faile, continues his relentless hunt for the Shaido who hold her.
recaps.in_short: As the Seanchan occupy Ebou Dar, Mat Cauthon recovers in hiding and is drawn to the enemy heir, Tuon, the Daughter of the Nine Moons, whom prophecy says he must marry. When his cover collapses he escapes the city in a daring flight, carrying Tuon away with him. Meanwhile Rand resolves to do the impossible: to cleanse the male half of the One Power of the Dark One's taint, the curse that drives men who channel mad. Gathering channelers and the immense sa'angreal called the Choedan Kal, and shielded by Nynaeve and a circle of allies, he channels a torrent of the Power at the tainted, evil-soaked ruins of Shadar Logoth, using one poison to burn out the other. Several of the Forsaken sense the vast weave and attack to stop him, and a desperate battle rages, but Rand succeeds. Saidin runs clean for the first time in three thousand years. Elayne, in Caemlyn, gathers support for her claim to Andor's throne, while Perrin's search for the captive Faile goes on.

recaps.text: Rand al'Thor, a young man from the isolated Two Rivers, was revealed as the Dragon Reborn, the rebirth of the champion who broke the world in the Age of Legends and is prophesied to fight the Dark One at the Last Battle. With his boyhood friends Mat and Perrin, both ta'veren who bend chance around them, and the village women Egwene and Nynaeve, he was drawn out of hiding by the Aes Sedai Moiraine into a world of channelers, prophecy, and war. Rand claimed the sword Callandor in Tear, crossed to the Aiel Waste and was accepted as their foretold leader, and took Cairhien and Illian, killing several of the Forsaken, the Dark One's freed lieutenants. He founded the Black Tower to train men who can channel as weapons for the Last Battle, despite the madness the tainted male Power brings. The Aes Sedai split: the White Tower under Elaida deposed and imprisoned the previous Amyrlin, while sisters who fled raised the young Egwene as a rival Amyrlin, now besieging Tar Valon. The invading Seanchan seized coastal cities and captured women who can channel to enslave them. Most recently Mat was buried under rubble during their attack on Ebou Dar, and Perrin's wife, Faile, was carried off by the renegade Shaido Aiel.

characters.description: The young witch of the Chalk, now thirteen, sent up into the mountains to continue her training with a succession of senior witches. Competent, stubborn, and used to being the person others rely on, she has grown into the daily work of witchcraft: nursing, midwifery, settling disputes, and doing the jobs nobody else will. She is also at an age where she wants to be noticed, which is a dangerous thing to be when the world is full of old stories looking for someone to act in them.
characters.name: Tiffany Aching

characters.description: The Big Man of the Nac Mac Feegle, the small blue fighting men of the Chalk, who consider Tiffany their hag and follow her wherever she goes. Reckless, loud, and entirely loyal, he has lately been struggling with two frightening new responsibilities: being a husband to the kelda and learning to read.
characters.name: Rob Anybody

characters.description: Rob Anybody's brother, cheerfully unburdened by thought, and the Feegle most likely to say the wrong thing at length. He means extremely well.
characters.name: Daft Wullie

characters.description: The kelda of the Chalk's Feegle mound and Rob Anybody's wife, small, sharp, and the real authority among the clan. She sees further than the warriors do and has become uneasy about how much of Tiffany's attention the Feegle still hold, and about what she senses coming.
characters.name: Jeannie

characters.description: The witch Tiffany is currently apprenticed to: one hundred and thirteen years old, blind and deaf, and dressed entirely in the fearsome black the villagers expect. She borrows the eyes and ears of animals to see and hear, holds court over local disputes with terrifying accuracy, and is respected and feared for miles. She has been a witch longer than anyone can remember and has strong opinions about what a witch owes the people around her.
characters.name: Miss Treason

characters.description: The elemental spirit of winter, who arrives each year to take the world from the Summer Lady in an ancient exchange danced out by the mountain villages. He is weather rather than a person: frost, ice, blizzard, and the shape of snowflakes. Until now he has never had cause to wonder what it might be like to be anything else.
characters.name: The Wintersmith

characters.description: The elemental spirit of summer, the Wintersmith's opposite and partner in the dance that turns the year. Where she walks, things grow.
characters.name: The Summer Lady

characters.description: The most formidable witch in the mountains, austere, unsentimental, and almost impossible to impress. She keeps a distant watch on Tiffany's progress, intervenes rarely and only where it will teach something, and is more interested in whether a young witch can get herself out of trouble than in getting her out of it.
characters.name: Granny Weatherwax

characters.description: A wandering witch-finder who searches schools and villages for girls with the talent, and who first found Tiffany. Bookish and brisk, she keeps track of her charges from a distance and worries about them more than she admits.
characters.name: Miss Tick

characters.description: A senior Lancre witch, cheerful, disreputable, and enormously experienced, with a large family and an extremely relaxed attitude to propriety. She is the witch people go to about births, marriages, and matters of the heart, and she understands the old stories about gods and elementals better than almost anyone.
characters.name: Nanny Ogg

characters.description: A young witch of Tiffany's age who leads the local circle of trainees by force of personality. Confident, imposing, and fluent in the vocabulary of magic, she is a great believer in the correct trappings and looks down on plain practical witchcraft.
characters.name: Annagramma Hawkin

characters.description: A shy, kind young witch of the same circle who specializes in pigs and is far tougher than she appears. She is Tiffany's steadiest friend among the trainees.
characters.name: Petulia Gristle

characters.description: The Baron's son from the Chalk, away at school, who writes to Tiffany and reads a great deal about heroes and quests. Awkward, sheltered, and pushed about by grasping relatives, he badly wants to be the sort of person the stories are about.
characters.name: Roland

characters.description: A cheese made by Tiffany that came out livelier than intended. Blue, hungry, and capable of surprising speed, it attaches itself to the Nac Mac Feegle, who consider it an excellent addition to the clan.
characters.name: Horace

characters.description: A minor goddess of things that stick in drawers, worshipped by rattling a stuck drawer and swearing. Recently promoted and enjoying it, she is easy to summon and free with advice.
characters.name: Anoia

recaps.ending: Winter refuses to end, burying the mountains and the Chalk under an enormous snowfall that kills livestock and traps whole villages, and the Wintersmith completes the human body he has been assembling out of the substances a man is made of, so that he can court Tiffany as a man. The Feegle, with Roland, reach the underworld and bring the Summer Lady back, along with a cornucopia that produces endless food, which is used to feed the snowbound. Tiffany goes to the Wintersmith's palace of ice and faces him. Because she has been carrying the Summer Lady's power since she stepped into the dance, she is able to give him what he has spent the book asking for: she accepts him and kisses him, and the heat she carries melts him away, ending the winter. The Summer Lady returns to take back her own role, and Tiffany hands the power over willingly, understanding at last that the seasons are a story that must be danced properly rather than improvised. Annagramma, propped up all year by Tiffany and the other trainees, finally learns that she has been helped and begins to make an honest job of her steading. Roland returns home a different young man, having gone into the underworld and come out again. Tiffany goes back to the Chalk older, steadier, and no longer interested in being noticed.
recaps.in_short: Tiffany Aching, thirteen and apprenticed to the ancient, blind Miss Treason, is taken to watch the dark, silent dance that turns the year from summer to winter, and, unable to stop herself, steps into it and dances with the Wintersmith. The elemental spirit of winter takes her for the Summer Lady, falls in love with her, and begins to court her with snowflakes shaped like her face, roses of ice, and icebergs carved into her likeness, while Tiffany finds that green shoots spring where she walks and that part of the Summer Lady's role has come to rest on her. Miss Treason dies at a time of her own choosing, and Tiffany moves to Nanny Ogg's while quietly holding together the steading her rival Annagramma has inherited. Winter deepens and will not end, because the story has been broken. The Wintersmith builds himself a human body to win her, the Nac Mac Feegle and Roland go down into the underworld to bring the Summer Lady back, and a great snowfall buries the Chalk. Tiffany goes to the Wintersmith's ice palace and ends him with the summer heat she has been carrying, giving the season back to its rightful owner.

recaps.text: Previously, in earlier books: Tiffany Aching, granddaughter of a much-loved Chalk shepherd, discovered she had a witch's talent while still a child. When her small brother was carried off by the Queen of the Fairies, she went into that country of dreams and brought him home, helped by the Nac Mac Feegle, the tiny blue fighting men who guard the Chalk and call her their hag. Sent into the mountains for a proper apprenticeship, she learned that real witchcraft is hard, humble, unpaid work for other people, and was caught and possessed by a hiver, an ancient mindless thing drawn to powerful minds. She freed herself by giving it what it had never had, an awareness of itself and of its own death, and in doing so earned the rare respect of Granny Weatherwax, the mountains' most formidable witch. Tiffany is now thirteen, still training away from home, still watched over by the Feegle, and increasingly aware that she is the Chalk's witch and that the Chalk is waiting for her to come back to it.

Tiffany is apprenticed to Miss Treason, a witch of one hundred and thirteen who is blind and deaf and gets around it by borrowing the senses of animals. Her cottage is full of clocks and skulls and everything else the villagers expect of a terrifying old witch, and she holds court over local quarrels with a judgement nobody dares argue with. She takes Tiffany to see the dark dance, an old, silent midwinter rite in which the village men dance the turning of the year and hand the world from the Summer Lady to the Wintersmith. Tiffany is told to watch and on no account to join in. Watching the two figures circle each other, she is caught by the shape of the thing, steps into the dance, and takes the Summer Lady's place opposite the Wintersmith. The dance closes over her, and something in the world's arrangements shifts.

The consequences begin at once. The Wintersmith has noticed Tiffany, and has taken her for the Summer Lady he is supposed to dance with. Snowflakes begin falling in the shape of her face, frost draws her likeness on windows, and winter arrives early and personally. Miss Treason, Miss Tick, and Granny Weatherwax all understand what has happened: Tiffany has walked into an old story that has been running since long before people, and stories of that kind do not care who is standing in the wrong place, they simply carry on. Part of the Summer Lady's role has come to rest on Tiffany, and the real Summer Lady is somewhere she should not be. The Feegle, who have followed Tiffany into the mountains as usual, take the view that the problem can be solved by hitting it, and are told that this particular problem is made of weather.

Miss Treason, who has always known exactly how long she has, announces the day of her death, holds her own funeral party for the whole district, and dies at the time she chose. Tiffany moves down to Lancre to stay with Nanny Ogg, who is cheerfully expert in the sort of trouble Tiffany is now in and explains that the Wintersmith is courting her. Miss Treason's cottage and steading go not to Tiffany but to Annagramma, the domineering leader of the local circle of young witches, who has been trained in theory and knows nothing whatever about the practical business of looking after frightened, poor, dying people. Meanwhile summer follows Tiffany about: green shoots spring up where her feet touch the ground, and she cannot make it stop. The Wintersmith's courtship becomes larger and stranger, running to roses of ice and icebergs shaped like her, and he begins to wonder what he would have to do to meet her as a man.

Winter settles in and will not move on, because the year's story has been broken and the Summer Lady is not where she should be. Tiffany, working out of Nanny Ogg's cottage, quietly organizes Petulia and the other trainees into propping Annagramma up without ever letting her know, taking on the night calls and the deaths and the difficult neighbours that Annagramma cannot handle. The Feegle, with Rob Anybody struggling to explain any of it to Jeannie, begin planning a raid on the underworld to fetch the Summer Lady back. The Wintersmith, working from an old song about what a man is made of, starts gathering the substances of a human body so that he can build himself one and be the kind of suitor Tiffany might accept. Granny Weatherwax makes it plain that nobody else can finish this: Tiffany stepped into the dance and Tiffany will have to step out of it.

Roland, home from school and tired of being the boy in the story who never does anything, goes down into the underworld with the Feegle to bring the Summer Lady out, and comes back with her and with a cornucopia, a horn that produces endless food and is very hard to switch off. Above ground the winter turns lethal. An enormous snowfall buries the mountains and reaches the Chalk, killing sheep, blocking roads, and burying farms and the people in them, and the witches spend themselves digging out survivors while the cornucopia feeds those who are cut off. The Wintersmith, now walking about in a body of his own making, comes looking for Tiffany, and Tiffany understands that he cannot be argued with, frightened off, or fought, because he is not a person who wants something, he is winter itself with a person's idea stuck in it.

Tiffany goes out through the snow to the Wintersmith's palace of ice and lets him have what he has been asking for all year. Because she has been carrying the Summer Lady's power ever since she stepped into the dance, her acceptance is fatal to him: she takes his hand and kisses him, and the heat she holds melts him away, breaking the winter and letting the year move on. The Summer Lady comes back to claim her own role, and Tiffany gives the power up without argument, having learned what it costs to improvise in a story that is older than people. The thaw reaches the Chalk. Annagramma, discovering how much she has been carried, is left to build something honest out of her steading, and Tiffany's part in it is finally acknowledged. Roland returns from the underworld visibly older and no longer willing to be pushed around by his relatives, and Tiffany goes home to the Chalk with the year running properly again and no further interest in being the girl everybody is looking at.

characters.description: Representing the Akura clan in the final stages of the Uncrowned King tournament, Lindon is an Underlord who fights with Blackflame, pure and empty madra, Soulsmith constructs, and the rapid analysis of his mind-spirit Dross. Having already outperformed every expectation for a competitor of his humble origins, he faces the tournament's strongest surviving competitors while still relying on preparation and adaptability rather than the inherited power of the great clans.
characters.name: Lindon

characters.description: One of the Akura team's fiercest competitors and Lindon's closest companion, a sword artist trained by the late Sage of the Endless Sword. She fights with blistering sword madra, the Endless Sword technique, and a blood shadow drawn from her own life, and she has carved her way through the tournament on skill and sheer will. She enters its final rounds determined to face the strongest opponents in the field, whatever the cost.
characters.name: Yerin

characters.description: The Arelius family sacred artist who teaches and patronizes Lindon and Yerin, guiding the Akura team with unshakeable good cheer and a mastery of Hollow and Void arts far beyond what his manner suggests. He shepherds his students through the tournament's conclusion with aims he keeps largely to himself.
characters.name: Eithan Arelius

characters.description: A kind-hearted princess of the Akura clan competing beside Lindon and Yerin, who wields the living shadow-bow known as the Book of Eternal Night. Loyal to her friends despite the demands of her ruthless family, she fights on into the tournament's final stages.
characters.name: Akura Mercy

characters.description: The quick-witted mind-spirit dwelling within Lindon, recovered from Ghostwater, who models opponents and dissects techniques faster than any person can think. His analysis is one of Lindon's decisive advantages in the tournament's hardest matches.
characters.name: Dross

characters.description: A golden dragon backed by the lion Monarch Reigan Shen and one of the tournament's most powerful and arrogant competitors. Contemptuous of anyone she deems lesser than a dragon, she is willing to go far beyond the bounds of a fair contest to see Lindon's group destroyed.
characters.name: Sopharanatoth

characters.description: The lion Monarch who patronizes the dragons and manipulates events around the tournament for his own long-term ambitions. Immensely powerful and coldly calculating, he is content to bend or break the contest's rules through his proxies to advance his aims.
characters.name: Reigan Shen

characters.description: One of the continent's reclusive Monarchs, a peerless hunter and scholar of the sacred arts who observes the young competitors with unusual attention. Detached from the politics of the other great powers, he takes a particular interest in Lindon over the course of the tournament.
characters.name: Northstrider

recaps.ending: Wintersteel closes with the Uncrowned King tournament finished and its two Akura underdogs remade. Yerin, nearly killed by the dragon Sopharanatoth's forbidden use of power, has claimed the complete legacy of the Sage of the Endless Sword and advanced into a far higher and harder state of strength, turning the dragons' attempt to destroy her into their public humiliation. Lindon's true significance has been exposed to the continent's rulers: the Monarchs recognize that his origins and his ties to forces from beyond Cradle make him far more than the backwater competitor he appeared to be, and the reclusive Monarch Northstrider has taken him on as a personal student. The dragons and their patron, the lion Monarch Reigan Shen, leave the tournament set back and humiliated but with their ambitions intact. Lindon and Yerin part from the contest dramatically stronger and now firmly within the sight of the great powers, while the larger dangers overshadowing Cradle - the ancient dreadgods and the schemes of the Monarchs - rise to the fore. The path ahead points away from tournaments and toward far greater and more perilous conflicts.
recaps.in_short: In the concluding half of the Uncrowned King tournament, Lindon, Yerin, and Mercy fight through the contest's most dangerous final rounds against the strongest young artists of the continent. When the golden dragon Sopharanatoth and her backers channel forbidden power to destroy Yerin, they gravely wound her but provoke a crisis that forces the watching Monarchs to intervene. Pushed to her limit, Yerin embraces the full legacy of the Sage of the Endless Sword and advances into a far greater state of power, turning the dragons' overreach into their humiliation. Meanwhile the Monarchs perceive that Lindon is far more than a backwater competitor, and his connection to forces from beyond Cradle comes to light, marking him as a figure of extraordinary interest. By the tournament's end the reclusive Monarch Northstrider has taken Lindon as his personal student, and both Lindon and Yerin emerge transformed and vastly stronger. Reigan Shen and the dragons are set back but undeterred, and the greater threats facing Cradle move to the center of the story.

recaps.text: Previously: after being warned that Cradle itself was in peril, Lindon left the backward region of Sacred Valley and climbed from the lowest rung of the sacred arts to Underlord, taking up Blackflame and a Path of pure and empty madra. He gathered companions - the sword artist Yerin, the secretly formidable Eithan Arelius, and the Akura princess Mercy - and won powerful tools and the mind-spirit Dross along the way, drawing the notice of the continent's Monarchs. Lindon, Yerin, and Mercy were entered as the Akura clan's representatives in the Uncrowned King tournament, a contest among the strongest young sacred artists of the great powers overseen by the Monarchs themselves. Against every expectation, Lindon and Yerin fought their way through the tournament's earlier rounds, earning the serious attention of the watching elders while making enemies of the golden dragons backed by the lion Monarch Reigan Shen, chief among them Sopharanatoth. Wintersteel opens with the tournament's decisive final rounds still to be fought.

The Uncrowned King tournament enters its final stages, and the matches between the last surviving competitors grow far more dangerous than the earlier rounds. Lindon and Yerin continue to defy the expectations placed on the Akura clan's lower-born entrants, advancing against prodigies from the continent's greatest powers. The hostility between the Akura team and the dragons sharpens, and the Monarchs watching the contest - including the reclusive hunter Northstrider - pay increasing attention to Lindon in particular. The stakes of the remaining matches rise as it becomes clear that some competitors, and their powerful patrons, intend far more than an honorable defeat of their rivals.

As the tournament narrows toward its strongest contenders, the danger to the competitors escalates sharply. Yerin is drawn toward a confrontation with the golden dragon Sopharanatoth, who is prepared to reach well past the limits of a fair contest to destroy her. The dragons' patron, Reigan Shen, works behind the scenes to tilt events in his faction's favor. Lindon pushes his Paths and his tools to their limits against opponents of tremendous power, while the Monarchs' oversight of the tournament is strained by the willingness of the great powers to bend its rules. The contest becomes less a game and more a proving ground where lives are genuinely at risk.

The tournament reaches its most brutal matches. Yerin's fight against Sopharanatoth turns catastrophic when the dragon and her backers channel power far beyond what the contest allows, and Yerin is grievously wounded. The overreach throws the tournament into crisis and forces the watching Monarchs to intervene in the affairs of the young competitors. In the aftermath, Yerin is pushed to the very edge of her strength and to a decision about how far she is willing to go to survive and to win, drawing on the full legacy left to her by the Sage of the Endless Sword.

Driven to her limit, Yerin embraces the complete inheritance of her master's Path and undergoes a profound advancement, hardening into a new and far greater state of power. The dragons' attempt to destroy her rebounds, and their faction is humiliated before the assembled powers. At the same time, scrutiny falls hard on Lindon: the Monarchs perceive that there is far more to him and his origins than a competitor from a backwater should possess, and his connection to forces from beyond Cradle begins to come to light, marking him out as a figure of extraordinary interest and concern among the most powerful beings on the continent.

With Lindon's hidden significance exposed, the Monarchs move to understand or lay claim to him. Northstrider, the reclusive hunter-Monarch who has watched Lindon throughout the tournament, takes him on as a personal student, placing Lindon under the tutelage of one of the most powerful and independent figures on the continent. The tournament's results are settled, the dragons and Reigan Shen's schemes are set back, and both Lindon and Yerin emerge from the contest transformed, far stronger than they began and now firmly in the sight of the great powers.

By the end of Wintersteel, the Uncrowned King tournament is concluded. Yerin has risen to a dramatically higher level of power through the full legacy of the Sage of the Endless Sword, and Lindon has become the student of the Monarch Northstrider, his connection to forces from beyond Cradle now known to the continent's rulers. The dragons and their patron Reigan Shen have been humbled, but their ambitions are undimmed, and the larger dangers looming over Cradle - the ancient dreadgods and the maneuvering of the Monarchs - move to the fore. Lindon and his companions leave the tournament changed and elevated, their path set toward far greater conflicts than any contest.
